question: A developer has an Appium suite and wants to write and debug it from a local IDE against a specific real iPhone in AWS Device Farm, with live logs and breakpoints. Which Device Farm capability fits?
choices: A Device Farm remote access session that uses the managed Appium endpoint
A Device Farm automated Appium test run on service-managed test hosts, uploaded as a test package
The Device Farm built-in fuzz test, run against the iPhone with a randomizer seed
A Device Farm custom test environment that uses a test spec file to configure the test host
explanation: In a remote access session, Device Farm exposes a managed Appium endpoint for the device. The developer can run Appium tests from a local client, with any language or IDE, live debugging with breakpoints, and live video and logs.

choiceExplanations.1: Automated runs upload the app and tests and execute them on Device Farm's managed test hosts (server-side), so the developer cannot debug live from a local IDE.
choiceExplanations.2: The fuzz test sends random user interface events and needs no scripts; it is not a way to debug an Appium suite.
choiceExplanations.3: A test spec file configures the test host for server-side runs; it does not connect a local IDE to a device.

resources.title: Appium testing in AWS Device Farm

question:
A company's Windows users in a branch office open shared files over SMB and sign in with their Active Directory accounts. The company wants the files stored as objects in Amazon S3, with recently used files cached locally.
Which AWS service should it use?
choices: AWS DataSync
AWS Storage Gateway
AWS Transfer Family
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
explanation: AWS Storage Gateway with an S3 File Gateway lets clients store and retrieve objects in S3 through SMB or NFS file shares, with transparent local caching. An SMB file share can use Active Directory to authenticate users.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DataSync is a file transfer service that moves data to, from and between AWS storage services. It copies data; it does not present an SMB share that users sign in to, backed by S3, with a local cache.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Transfer Family offers managed file transfer over SFTP, FTPS, FTP, AS2 and browser-based transfers into storage such as Amazon S3. SMB file shares with Active Directory sign-in and a local cache are not what it provides.
choiceExplanations.3: FSx for Windows File Server gives SMB file shares and works with Active Directory, but the files live in its own Windows file system. They are not stored as objects in Amazon S3.

resources.title: Use Active Directory to authenticate users
What is Amazon S3 File Gateway

question:
A company uses AWS Storage Gateway for application servers that need iSCSI block volumes. The primary copy of the data must live in Amazon S3, and only frequently accessed data should stay on premises so it avoids buying more local disks.
Which gateway configuration should the company deploy?
choices: S3 File Gateway with an NFS file share
Volume Gateway with stored volumes
Tape Gateway with a virtual tape library
Volume Gateway with cached volumes
explanation: Cached volumes store the data in Amazon S3 as the primary copy and keep a local copy of frequently accessed data for low-latency access. They are attached to servers as iSCSI devices, and they reduce the need to scale on-premises storage.

choiceExplanations.0: S3 File Gateway gives file access to S3 objects through NFS or SMB. The servers need iSCSI block volumes, which is what Volume Gateway provides.
choiceExplanations.1: With stored volumes the whole dataset is kept on premises and only point-in-time snapshots are backed up asynchronously to S3. The primary copy stays local, so local disk needs stay high.
choiceExplanations.2: Tape Gateway provides virtual tape storage for archiving backup data. It does not present general-purpose iSCSI volumes whose primary copy is in S3.

question:
A video-production firm's editors use an NFS share on an on-premises NAS that is being decommissioned. Finished projects must be stored in Amazon S3 as ordinary objects that cloud rendering jobs read through the S3 API. Recently opened files must still open quickly at the studio, and projects should move to an archive storage class automatically as they age.
As the solutions architect, which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
choices: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with cached volumes, plus an S3 Lifecycle rule on the bucket that holds the volume data
An AWS DataSync task that copies the NFS share to Amazon S3 every hour, plus an S3 Lifecycle rule for old projects
AWS Storage Gateway S3 File Gateway with an NFS share at the studio, plus an S3 Lifecycle rule for archiving
Amazon EFS mounted at the studio over AWS Direct Connect, plus EFS lifecycle management for older files
explanation: S3 File Gateway exposes S3 objects as NFS or SMB shares, caches recently used data locally, and keeps the data accessible directly in S3 from AWS applications. The bucket can be managed with S3 lifecycle policies.

choiceExplanations.0: Volume Gateway stores its volume data in S3, but you can't access that data with the S3 API, so the rendering jobs could not read the projects as objects. It also presents iSCSI block volumes rather than an NFS share.
choiceExplanations.1: DataSync copies data between storage systems; it does not serve an NFS share. With the NAS being decommissioned, the editors would have no share to open files from and no local cache of recent files.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon EFS is a separate NFS file system. The finished projects would not be ordinary S3 objects that the rendering jobs read through the S3 API.

resources.title: What is Amazon S3 File Gateway

question:
An S3 File Gateway serves an SMB share for a branch office from an Amazon S3 bucket. A data pipeline in AWS now writes new objects straight into the same bucket, but branch users do not see the new files in the share.
Which TWO actions can make the gateway show the new files? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Add more cache disks to the S3 File Gateway virtual machine
Turn on automated cache refresh, using a TTL, on the S3 File Gateway file share
Turn on S3 Versioning for the bucket behind the S3 File Gateway
Change the S3 File Gateway file share's default storage class to S3 Standard-IA
Run a RefreshCache operation for the S3 File Gateway file share
explanation: A gateway does not automatically notice objects uploaded directly to its bucket, so its cached inventory of objects must be refreshed. You can run a RefreshCache operation (manually, or on a schedule you set up), or turn on automated cache refresh with a time-to-live value.

choiceExplanations.0: Cache disks hold file data for low-latency access. The problem is the gateway's cached inventory of objects, which is not updated automatically for objects uploaded directly to S3, and more disk space does not refresh it.
choiceExplanations.2: Versioning keeps multiple versions of objects. It does not make the gateway rescan the bucket, and changes made directly to a versioned bucket can even change what the share shows.
choiceExplanations.3: A storage class setting has no bearing on the gateway's cached inventory of the bucket, which is the part that is out of date.

resources.title: Refreshing Amazon S3 bucket object cache

question:
A SaaS provider gives each customer its own Aurora MySQL cluster. Each customer's load rises and falls during the day, and engineers spend hours every week resizing the writer and reader instances by hand.
Which Aurora option removes this capacity management for every cluster?
choices: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas
Amazon Aurora provisioned instances
Amazon Aurora Global Database
explanation: Aurora Serverless v2 scales each writer and reader automatically within a minimum and maximum capacity range, so nobody picks or changes instance classes. It is described as well suited to multitenant setups with one cluster per tenant.

choiceExplanations.1: Aurora Auto Scaling adjusts only the number of Aurora Replicas and does not apply to the writer, so the writer still has to be resized by hand.
choiceExplanations.2: With provisioned instances you choose an instance class and manually change it when the workload changes, so the engineers would still be resizing.
choiceExplanations.3: Aurora Global Database spreads a cluster across Regions for disaster recovery and local reads. It does not change how each instance's compute capacity is managed.

question:
A team is moving an Aurora cluster to Aurora Serverless v2 so that database capacity follows demand automatically. During setup, the team must define how far each writer and reader is allowed to scale.
Which setting does the team configure?
choices: Aurora Auto Scaling minimum and maximum number of Aurora Replicas
Aurora Serverless v2 minimum and maximum capacity, measured in ACUs
Aurora DB instance class chosen for the writer and each reader
Aurora Serverless v2 reader promotion tier
explanation: For each cluster you define a capacity range in Aurora capacity units (ACUs), a minimum and a maximum. Aurora Serverless v2 scales each writer and reader within that range.

choiceExplanations.0: That policy sets how many Aurora Replicas Aurora Auto Scaling may add or remove. It does not set how much capacity an instance can scale to.
choiceExplanations.2: Aurora Serverless v2 instances use the db.serverless class rather than a fixed size; their capacity is expressed in ACUs within the cluster's capacity range.
choiceExplanations.3: The promotion tier decides whether a reader's capacity follows the writer or scales independently, and which reader is promoted first on failover. It does not set the minimum and maximum capacity.

question:
A company runs production on Aurora PostgreSQL with large provisioned instances in us-east-1. It needs disaster recovery in eu-west-1 using Aurora's cross-Region replication, with minimal data loss. The DR Region takes no traffic until a failover, but then it must carry the full production load without anyone resizing instances. The company wants the lowest standby cost that meets these needs.
Which design should the company choose?
choices: Aurora Global Database with large provisioned instances matching production in the secondary cluster
Aurora Global Database with one small provisioned instance in the secondary cluster, resized after a failover
An Aurora Multi-AZ cluster with Aurora Replicas in three Availability Zones of us-east-1
Aurora Global Database with Aurora Serverless v2 instances in the secondary cluster
explanation: A secondary cluster in an Aurora global database may not need as much capacity as the primary until it is promoted. Using Aurora Serverless v2 instances there lets the cluster scale up when a secondary Region is promoted and takes over the workload.

choiceExplanations.0: This meets the capacity need, but it pays for production-sized instances around the clock in a Region that carries no traffic, so it is not the lowest standby cost.
choiceExplanations.1: The small instance would have to be resized after the failover, which is the manual step the company wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: A Multi-AZ cluster keeps the database running through an Availability Zone failure inside one Region. It does not provide a second Region for disaster recovery.

question:
An Aurora Serverless v2 cluster has one writer and one reader that exists mainly as the failover target. The writer scales up sharply during busy periods. After a failover, the promoted reader must already hold at least the capacity the writer had, without having to scale up first.
How should the reader be configured?
choices: Aurora Serverless v2 reader in promotion tier 15
Aurora Serverless v2 reader in promotion tier 7
Aurora Serverless v2 reader in promotion tier 1
Aurora Serverless v2 reader in promotion tier 3
explanation: For readers in promotion tiers 0 and 1, the minimum capacity follows the current writer capacity, so they are at least as large as the writer and can take over its workload on a failover.

choiceExplanations.0: Readers in promotion tiers 2 to 15 scale independently from the writer, so this reader can sit idle at low capacity while the writer is busy.
choiceExplanations.1: A reader in tiers 2 to 15 stays within the cluster's minimum and maximum capacity on its own, so it is not tied to the writer's current capacity.
choiceExplanations.3: Tiers 2 to 15 let a reader scale down while the writer keeps processing a high volume of transactions, and a reader promoted from there may need to scale up to handle the full workload.

question:
A publishing company stores articles as JSON documents whose fields differ from one article to the next. Developers query them with MongoDB aggregation pipelines and want automatic failover to replicas in other Availability Zones.
Which AWS database should the company use?
choices: Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Keyspaces
Amazon DocumentDB
Amazon Neptune
explanation: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed document database that works with MongoDB drivers and supports aggregation pipeline operators. Its cluster volume spans three Availability Zones, and replicas in other zones increase availability.

choiceExplanations.0: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database with its own APIs. The requirement to run MongoDB aggregation pipelines points to the MongoDB-compatible service.
choiceExplanations.1: Keyspaces is compatible with Apache Cassandra and its Cassandra Query Language, not with MongoDB.
choiceExplanations.3: Neptune is a graph database for highly connected data. It is not a MongoDB-compatible document store.

question:
An Amazon DocumentDB cluster has one primary instance, and read-only reporting queries from several applications now slow it down. The team wants to scale reads in the same Region without affecting how writes are handled.
Which DocumentDB option should the team use?
choices: A DocumentDB global cluster with a secondary Region
DocumentDB replica instances, reached through the reader endpoint
A larger instance class for the DocumentDB primary instance
DocumentDB cluster snapshots restored into a second cluster
explanation: Replica instances support only read operations and share the cluster volume, so they offload reads from the primary. The reader endpoint load balances read-only connections across the replicas.

choiceExplanations.0: A global cluster adds read-only clusters in other Regions for disaster recovery and local reads. The need is more read capacity in the same Region, so it adds cross-Region replication that is not needed.
choiceExplanations.2: A larger primary still serves reads and writes on the same instance, so the reporting queries keep competing with writes.
choiceExplanations.3: A snapshot is a point-in-time backup, and a restored cluster is a separate copy, so the reports would run on data that is not kept current.

question:
A social app stores hundreds of millions of user profiles as JSON documents and talks to its database through the MongoDB API. Peak traffic is expected to reach millions of writes per second, and the data will grow to petabytes. The team does not want to choose, size or patch database instances.
Which solution fits best?
choices: Amazon DocumentDB instance-based cluster with the largest instance class and 15 replicas
Amazon DynamoDB tables in on-demand capacity mode, with the profiles stored as items
A MongoDB sharded cluster on Amazon EC2 instances, managed by the application team
Amazon DocumentDB elastic cluster, with shards added as the workload grows
explanation: Elastic clusters support millions of reads and writes per second and petabytes of storage, and they remove the need to choose, manage or upgrade instances. They shard data across shards and use a MongoDB-compatible API.

choiceExplanations.0: An instance-based cluster has a single primary instance for writes, and its cluster volume is limited to 128 TiB (256 TiB with engine version 8.0), far below petabytes. The team would also still choose and size instances.
choiceExplanations.1: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database that scales, but the application talks to its database through the MongoDB API, which DocumentDB provides.
choiceExplanations.2: Self-managed MongoDB on EC2 means the team chooses, sizes and patches the instances itself, which it wants to avoid.

resources.title: Amazon DocumentDB elastic clusters: how it works

question:
Amazon DocumentDB stores a company's data in eu-west-1. A new resilience requirement says that if the Region fails, the application must recover in another Region with an RTO of about a minute and an RPO of seconds, while staff in ap-southeast-1 read the same data with local latency.
Which DocumentDB capability meets these requirements?
choices: A DocumentDB global cluster with a secondary cluster in ap-southeast-1
DocumentDB replica instances spread across three Availability Zones in eu-west-1
DocumentDB cluster snapshots copied to ap-southeast-1 and restored after an outage
A DocumentDB elastic cluster with extra shards placed in ap-southeast-1
explanation: A global cluster has a primary Region and read-only secondary Regions, with replication latency typically under a second. After a Region-wide outage a secondary can be promoted within minutes, with a typical RTO under a minute and an RPO typically measured in seconds, and secondary clusters serve local reads.

choiceExplanations.1: Replicas in separate Availability Zones improve availability inside one Region. A Region-wide outage still takes the whole cluster out, and nothing serves staff in ap-southeast-1.
choiceExplanations.2: A copied snapshot is a point-in-time backup, so recovery means restoring a new cluster and losing recent writes. A global cluster replicates continuously with typical latency under a second.
choiceExplanations.3: An elastic cluster keeps its data in one Region, and creating global clusters is listed among the features elastic clusters do not support.

resources.title: Overview of Amazon DocumentDB global clusters

question:
A logistics company stores parcel scan events in wide-column tables and reads them with the Cassandra Query Language (CQL) from existing application code. The team wants to stop patching database nodes and needs to restore a table to an earlier point in time.
Which AWS database should it move to?
choices: Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon DocumentDB
Amazon Neptune
Amazon Keyspaces
explanation: Amazon Keyspaces is a managed, serverless Apache Cassandra-compatible service with no servers to provision or patch, and it runs the same Cassandra application code. Point-in-time recovery lets you restore a table to an earlier point in time.

choiceExplanations.0: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database, but the requirement to keep CQL application code points to Keyspaces, the Cassandra-compatible service.
choiceExplanations.1: DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible and stores JSON documents. It does not run CQL application code.
choiceExplanations.2: Neptune is a graph database for highly connected data. It does not run CQL application code.

resources.title: What is Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)?
How point-in-time recovery works in Amazon Keyspaces

question:
A new Amazon Keyspaces table will serve a mobile game launch. Nobody can forecast the request rate, traffic will be spiky, and the team does not want to estimate or manage throughput capacity. The team prefers to pay per request.
Which Keyspaces setting should the team choose for the table?
choices: Keyspaces provisioned capacity mode with fixed read and write capacity units
Keyspaces multi-Region replication across two Regions
Keyspaces on-demand capacity mode for the table
Keyspaces Time to Live (TTL) default value on the table
explanation: On-demand mode serves thousands of requests per second without capacity planning and charges per request. It is a good option for new tables with unknown workloads and unpredictable traffic.

choiceExplanations.0: Provisioned mode needs you to specify the reads and writes per second the application requires. It suits predictable traffic that you can forecast.
choiceExplanations.1: Multi-Region replication copies tables to other Regions for resilience and local access. A multi-Region keyspace still needs a capacity mode, so it does not remove capacity planning.
choiceExplanations.3: TTL expires old data automatically to save storage. It does not change how read and write throughput is provisioned or billed.

question:
A mobile-game studio stores player inventory with CQL queries from existing application code. Players in Europe and Asia must read and write with single-digit-millisecond latency in their nearest Region, and the game must stay playable if one Region degrades. The studio wants the LEAST operational overhead and no conflict-resolution code of its own.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Amazon Keyspaces with a multi-Region keyspace replicated to both Regions
Apache Cassandra on Amazon EC2 instances in both Regions, using a multi-datacenter topology
An Amazon DocumentDB global cluster with a secondary cluster in the second Region
Amazon DynamoDB global tables with a replica table in each Region
explanation: Keyspaces multi-Region replication is fully managed and active-active, so each Region can read and write locally. Conflicts are resolved in the background with cell-level timestamps and last writer wins, and replication lag is typically under a second.

choiceExplanations.1: Self-managed Cassandra means the studio runs and patches nodes in both Regions, which is the operational overhead it wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: A DocumentDB global cluster accepts writes only in its primary Region, and DocumentDB is MongoDB-compatible rather than a CQL service.
choiceExplanations.3: DynamoDB global tables replicate across Regions, but DynamoDB is a different, non-Cassandra service; the existing CQL application code points to Keyspaces.

resources.title: Multi-Region replication for Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)

question:
An IoT platform keeps all device readings in one Amazon Keyspaces table because its queries span both kinds of rows. Most readings must be deleted automatically after 30 days, but readings flagged as compliance records must be kept for seven years. The team does not want to write or schedule delete jobs.
Which configuration should the team use?
choices: A Keyspaces table default TTL of 30 days, with no other TTL settings
A Keyspaces table default TTL of 30 days, with a longer custom TTL set on the compliance rows
Two Keyspaces tables, each with its own default TTL, and a job that moves flagged rows between them
Keyspaces point-in-time recovery on the table, restoring a new table when old rows must be removed
explanation: Keyspaces TTL expires data automatically. You can set a default TTL for the whole table and override it for individual rows and columns, so the flagged rows can keep a longer lifetime.

choiceExplanations.0: A table-wide default applies to every row, so the compliance readings would be deleted after 30 days as well.
choiceExplanations.2: This breaks the requirement to keep the readings in one table and adds a job to build and run, which the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.3: Point-in-time recovery provides continuous backups from which a table can be restored to a new table. It does not delete data automatically.

resources.title: Expire data with Time to Live (TTL) for Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra)

question:
An infrastructure team wants to map how servers, applications, databases and teams depend on each other, so it can see what is affected if a database goes down by following links through many levels. Answers must return in milliseconds over billions of relationships.
Which AWS service fits?
choices: Amazon Redshift
Amazon DocumentDB
Amazon Neptune
Amazon DynamoDB
explanation: Neptune is a fully managed graph database for highly connected datasets, optimized for storing billions of relationships and querying the graph with millisecond latency.

choiceExplanations.0: Redshift is a petabyte-scale data warehouse for analytics. It is not a graph database built for following relationships through many levels.
choiceExplanations.1: DocumentDB is a MongoDB-compatible database for JSON documents, not a graph database.
choiceExplanations.3: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database for operational workloads. It is not a purpose-built graph database for following links through many levels.

question:
A company keeps a graph in Amazon Neptune and a search index of the same data elsewhere. Every graph change must be delivered in the exact order it was made, with no duplicates, through an HTTP API, so a reader application can update the index.
Which Neptune feature provides this?
choices: Neptune Streams
Neptune read replicas
Neptune global database
Neptune cluster snapshots
explanation: Neptune Streams logs every change to the graph in the order it is made, with no duplicates, and the change records are retrieved with an HTTP REST API. One use case is keeping a current copy of the graph in another store such as Amazon OpenSearch Service.

choiceExplanations.1: Read replicas add read capacity for queries against the graph. They do not provide an ordered log of every change.
choiceExplanations.2: A global database replicates the cluster to read-only secondary clusters in other Regions. It does not expose an ordered change log over an HTTP API.
choiceExplanations.3: Snapshots are point-in-time backups of the cluster volume. They do not deliver each change as it happens.

resources.title: Capturing graph changes in real time using Neptune streams

question:
A cloud security team models its accounts, roles, instances, buckets and network paths as connected data. Analysts must run path queries such as which internet-facing instance can reach a bucket holding customer data through any chain of roles, with answers in milliseconds over billions of relationships. The database must stay available if an Availability Zone fails and must not need server management.
Which solution fits?
choices: Amazon Redshift with a Multi-AZ deployment, storing each relationship as a row joined by SQL
Amazon OpenSearch Service across three Availability Zones, storing each relationship as a document
Amazon DynamoDB with global tables, storing each relationship as an item
Amazon Neptune with a read replica in a second Availability Zone
explanation: Neptune is built for highly connected data and stores billions of relationships with millisecond queries. A read replica in a different Availability Zone is a failover target, so Neptune can promote it if the primary fails.

choiceExplanations.0: Redshift Multi-AZ keeps the data warehouse running through an Availability Zone failure, but Redshift is built for analytic SQL, not for traversing billions of relationships in milliseconds.
choiceExplanations.1: OpenSearch is a search and analytics engine for uses such as log analytics. It is not a graph database for following chains of relationships.
choiceExplanations.2: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database for operational workloads. Following an unbounded chain of relationships would mean many separate lookups, not graph queries.

resources.title: Amazon Neptune DB Clusters and Instances

question:
Production graph data lives in an Amazon Neptune cluster in us-east-1. The company now needs disaster recovery in eu-west-1 with an RPO and RTO of minutes at most, and its European office wants to read the graph with local latency. The company wants the LEAST operational overhead.
Which option should it use?
choices: A Neptune global database with a secondary cluster in eu-west-1
Cross-Region snapshot copy and restore into eu-west-1
Neptune Streams with a replication application that keeps a standby cluster in eu-west-1 in sync
A Neptune read replica in a second Availability Zone of us-east-1
explanation: A Neptune global database has a primary cluster and read-only secondary clusters in other Regions, with replication typically under a second and local reads in the secondary Regions. Streams-based replication and snapshot copy are the alternatives, with more overhead or slower recovery.

choiceExplanations.1: Copying a full snapshot between Regions can take significant transfer time, so this approach suits an RPO and RTO of hours, not minutes.
choiceExplanations.2: This can bring RPO and RTO down to minutes, but the operational overhead of maintaining the replication components, and of running a second cluster all the time, can be significant.
choiceExplanations.3: A replica in another Availability Zone protects against a zone failure inside one Region. It gives no recovery in eu-west-1 and no local reads for the European office.

resources.title: Using Amazon Neptune with a global database

question:
A marketing team runs complex SQL joins and aggregations on terabytes of campaign data to feed BI dashboards, but only for a few hours each day. The team wants a columnar data warehouse with no clusters to size or manage, and it wants to pay only for the capacity it uses.
Which service fits best?
choices: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
Amazon EMR Serverless
Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
Amazon Redshift Serverless
explanation: Amazon Redshift Serverless automatically provisions and scales data warehouse capacity, and you pay only for the capacity you use. Existing BI tools keep working without changes.

choiceExplanations.0: Aurora Serverless v2 is an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration of Aurora, a relational database engine. It is not a columnar data warehouse for analytics.
choiceExplanations.1: EMR Serverless runs open-source frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hive for data processing jobs without clusters to manage. It is not a managed data warehouse for BI dashboards.
choiceExplanations.2: OpenSearch Serverless automatically scales an OpenSearch search and analytics engine. It is not a data warehouse for SQL joins and aggregations feeding BI dashboards.

question:
A company's Amazon Redshift data warehouse feeds executive dashboards and must keep running if an entire Availability Zone fails. The team wants applications to keep using one endpoint and does not want to restore anything from a backup.
Which Redshift option meets this?
choices: Redshift Multi-AZ deployment on RA3 nodes
Redshift cross-Region snapshot copy
Redshift concurrency scaling
Redshift Spectrum
explanation: A Multi-AZ deployment runs compute resources in two Availability Zones behind a single endpoint. If one zone fails, Redshift keeps operating on the remaining zone's resources, though connections must be re-established.

choiceExplanations.1: Copied snapshots are backups; restoring one creates a new cluster, which is the restore step the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: Concurrency scaling is a performance option for handling concurrent queries. It does not put compute in a second Availability Zone.
choiceExplanations.3: Spectrum lets the cluster query data that is already in Amazon S3. It does not add compute in a second Availability Zone.

question:
A ride-hailing app publishes trip events to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Analysts must join the events with customer and driver tables and run complex SQL aggregations over years of history for BI dashboards, with new events queryable within minutes. An Amazon Data Firehose stream will deliver the events.
Which destination should the Firehose stream use?
choices: Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon Redshift
Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon Athena
explanation: Redshift is a data warehouse for SQL joins and aggregations with BI tools, and it is a Firehose destination. Firehose delivers the data to an intermediate S3 bucket and then issues a COPY command to load it into Redshift.

choiceExplanations.0: OpenSearch is a supported Firehose destination, but it is a search and log-analytics engine, not a data warehouse for joining years of history with dimension tables in complex SQL aggregations for BI.
choiceExplanations.2: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database for operational workloads. It is not among the destinations a Firehose stream can deliver to.
choiceExplanations.3: Athena is a query service for data in S3. It is not among the destinations a Firehose stream can deliver to.

question:
A bank loads daily files from an Amazon S3 bucket into its Amazon Redshift cluster with the COPY command. The security team requires that this traffic stays inside the company's VPC, so that it can be controlled with VPC endpoint policies and monitored with VPC flow logs, rather than being routed over the internet.
Which TWO steps meet this requirement? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Turn on enhanced VPC routing for the Redshift cluster
Set the Redshift cluster as not publicly accessible and place it in private subnets
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the cluster's VPC
Encrypt the Redshift cluster with a customer managed AWS KMS key
Deliver Redshift database audit logs to an S3 bucket
explanation: Enhanced VPC routing forces all COPY and UNLOAD traffic between the cluster and data repositories through your VPC, so you can use security groups, network ACLs, VPC endpoints with endpoint policies, and flow logs. You must also create a network path, such as a VPC endpoint for a bucket in the same Region, or the COPY command can fail.

choiceExplanations.1: Without enhanced VPC routing, Redshift routes COPY and UNLOAD traffic through the internet, including traffic to other AWS services, regardless of how the cluster is placed.
choiceExplanations.3: Encryption protects the data itself. The route the COPY traffic takes is decided by enhanced VPC routing, not by encryption.
choiceExplanations.4: Audit logging records activity on the cluster. It does not change the network path of COPY traffic.

resources.title: Controlling network traffic with Redshift enhanced VPC routing

question:
An online store wants shoppers to find products by typing part of any word in a name or description, including partial matches, across millions of items. The catalog data itself lives in another database.
Which AWS service should provide the search?
choices: Amazon Athena queries over files in S3
Amazon OpenSearch Service
An Amazon Redshift data warehouse
Amazon DynamoDB table scans
explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed search and analytics engine that can search any field, including partial matches, and it is commonly used as a complement to another database that holds the source data.

choiceExplanations.0: Athena runs interactive SQL queries on data in S3 for analysis. It is not a search engine for a shopper-facing search box.
choiceExplanations.2: Redshift is a data warehouse for analytic SQL queries, not a search engine for a shopper-facing search box.
choiceExplanations.3: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database for operational workloads; it is not a search engine.

question:
A startup uses Amazon OpenSearch Service to search its support articles. Searches arrive in unpredictable bursts for a few hours a day, and the team does not want to choose instance types or node counts.
Which OpenSearch option should the startup use?
choices: A provisioned OpenSearch Service domain with fixed data nodes
An OpenSearch Service domain with UltraWarm nodes
An OpenSearch Serverless collection for the search workload
An OpenSearch Service domain with Cognito authentication for Dashboards
explanation: OpenSearch Serverless is an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration. A collection scales compute automatically, which suits infrequent, intermittent or unpredictable workloads without manual capacity management.

choiceExplanations.0: A provisioned domain is built from the instance types and counts that you specify, which is the sizing work the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.1: UltraWarm is a lower-cost storage tier for read-only data. The domain still has instance types and counts to choose.
choiceExplanations.3: Cognito authentication controls who can sign in to OpenSearch Dashboards. It does not change how capacity is managed.

question:
An order system stores orders in Amazon DynamoDB, which can be queried only by key or index. Support agents now need to find orders by any field, including partial matches inside free-text notes, and new orders must become searchable within seconds. The solution must not add read load to the table.
Which solution should the architect choose?
choices: A global secondary index on each attribute agents search, queried with Query requests
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the table, with agents searching through DAX
Amazon Athena queries over a nightly DynamoDB export to Amazon S3, run by agents
Amazon OpenSearch Service, updated from the table's DynamoDB stream by an AWS Lambda function
explanation: OpenSearch can search any field, including partial matches. A DynamoDB stream triggers a Lambda function that indexes each new or changed item, so the search stays current without reading the table.

choiceExplanations.0: A global secondary index is queried by key attributes with Query requests. It does not search for partial words inside free-text notes.
choiceExplanations.1: DAX is an in-memory cache that speeds up reads of eventually consistent data. It adds no partial-match text search, and agents searching through it would still read the table's items.
choiceExplanations.2: An export gives a point-in-time copy of the table in S3 that Athena can query. A nightly cycle cannot make new orders searchable within seconds.

resources.title: Loading streaming data from Amazon DynamoDB

question:
A security team keeps 18 months of application logs in an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Only the newest two weeks are searched often. Older indexes are read-only and queried rarely, but analysts must still be able to search them in OpenSearch Dashboards. The team wants to cut storage cost without losing that ability.
Which approach should it use?
choices: OpenSearch automated snapshots, deleting old indexes and restoring them when analysts need them
OpenSearch UltraWarm storage, with an Index State Management policy that moves older indexes
More hot data nodes and an extra replica for every index in the domain
Dedicated master nodes added to the OpenSearch domain
explanation: UltraWarm stores large amounts of read-only data on Amazon S3 with caching at significantly lower cost per GiB, and warm indexes can be queried with the same APIs and used in OpenSearch Dashboards. Index State Management is the recommended way to migrate indexes automatically once they reach a certain age.

choiceExplanations.0: Snapshots back up and restore a domain, but deleted indexes cannot be searched in Dashboards until they have been restored, which loses the required ability.
choiceExplanations.2: Hot storage carries overhead for replicas and reserved space, so this increases cost instead of cutting it.
choiceExplanations.3: Dedicated master nodes offload cluster management tasks. They do not reduce the cost of storing old data.

resources.title: UltraWarm storage for Amazon OpenSearch Service

question:
A company's data center sends a steady, high-volume data feed to applications in a VPC. The traffic must not cross the public internet, and the company wants consistent network latency that internet paths cannot guarantee.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Client VPN
AWS PrivateLink
explanation: AWS Direct Connect links the data center to AWS over a dedicated connection and lets you create virtual interfaces to a VPC, bypassing internet service providers. Internet latency varies as routes change, while Direct Connect offers consistent, low-latency connectivity.

choiceExplanations.0: Site-to-Site VPN encrypts traffic with IPsec tunnels, but the tunnels run over an internet connection, so latency can still vary with internet routing.
choiceExplanations.2: Client VPN is a managed client-based VPN that individual users reach with OpenVPN-based clients; it is not a link for a data center.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS PrivateLink connects a VPC privately to services and resources, such as endpoint services in other VPCs; it is not a physical link from a data center.

question:
A company has one Direct Connect connection to a Direct Connect location in us-east-1. It now has VPCs in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1, all in the same account, and wants to reach both VPCs over this single connection.
What should the company set up?
choices: A Direct Connect gateway associated with a private virtual interface
A Direct Connect public virtual interface that is shared by both VPCs
A second Direct Connect connection ordered at a location in eu-west-1
A Direct Connect link aggregation group made from the existing connection
explanation: A private virtual interface can connect to a Direct Connect gateway, a globally available resource that can reach VPCs in any Region except the AWS China Regions. The VPCs are associated with the gateway through their virtual private gateways.

choiceExplanations.1: A public virtual interface gives access to public AWS services over public IP addresses; it does not provide private access to VPCs.
choiceExplanations.2: The company wants to use its existing connection, and a Direct Connect gateway already lets that connection reach VPCs in other Regions, so a second connection is not needed.
choiceExplanations.3: A link aggregation group only groups connections that end on the same AWS device to add bandwidth; it does not add access to VPCs in another Region.

question:
A video production studio renders frames on a farm in its own data center. Every night the farm reads and writes a very large volume of data in Amazon S3. Security policy forbids sending this traffic over the public internet, and the studio wants predictable throughput. The network team can wait several weeks for the circuit.
Which solution should the studio choose?
choices: AWS Site-to-Site VPN to a virtual private gateway, with an S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC
AWS Direct Connect with a private virtual interface, with an S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC
AWS Direct Connect with a public virtual interface, used to reach the Amazon S3 public endpoints
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration, used over the studio's existing internet connection
explanation: A Direct Connect public virtual interface provides access to public AWS services such as Amazon S3 over the dedicated connection instead of the internet. Gateway endpoints cannot be used from on premises, so the two options that rely on one cannot work for the data center.

choiceExplanations.0: A Site-to-Site VPN runs over an internet connection, and an S3 gateway endpoint does not allow access from on premises.
choiceExplanations.1: A private virtual interface reaches the VPC, but an S3 gateway endpoint does not allow access from on premises, so the farm cannot use it to reach Amazon S3.
choiceExplanations.3: Transfer Acceleration is used over the studio's existing internet connection, which the security policy forbids.

question:
A trading firm runs a critical workload over AWS Direct Connect. It wants to order the topology that AWS ties to the 99.99% SLA, so that the failure of one device or of an entire Direct Connect location cannot take down the connection.
Which design should the firm order?
choices: Two Direct Connect connections that end on separate devices in a single Direct Connect location
A link aggregation group of Direct Connect connections at one Direct Connect location
Two Direct Connect connections, one at each of two different Direct Connect locations
Separate Direct Connect connections that end on separate devices at more than one location
explanation: The maximum resiliency model, which targets the 99.99% SLA, uses separate connections that terminate on separate devices in more than one location. It protects against device, connectivity and complete location failures.

choiceExplanations.0: Separate connections on separate devices in one location is the development and test model for non-critical workloads, and it does not survive the loss of the location.
choiceExplanations.1: A link aggregation group only includes ports on the same AWS device, and it is not recommended as a high-availability strategy.
choiceExplanations.2: One connection at each of two locations is the high resiliency model, which targets a 99.9% SLA rather than 99.99%.

question:
A company's branch office needs an encrypted connection to its VPC. The branch already has a business internet connection, and the company does not want to order a physical circuit or wait for one to be installed.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: AWS Direct Connect
AWS PrivateLink
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Client VPN
explanation: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec VPN connections between the branch network and the VPC, using the branch's existing internet connection, so no physical circuit is needed.

choiceExplanations.0: Direct Connect needs a physical connection at a Direct Connect location, either colocated or through a partner, so it requires a new circuit.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS PrivateLink gives a VPC private access to services and resources; it does not create an encrypted tunnel to a branch network.
choiceExplanations.3: Client VPN is a client-based VPN for individual users with OpenVPN-based clients, not for connecting a whole branch network.

question:
A company created an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to a virtual private gateway attached to its VPC. Both tunnels show as UP and the security groups allow the traffic, but servers in the data center cannot reach instances in the VPC's private subnets.
What should the company do?
choices: Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so the Site-to-Site VPN tunnels can carry traffic
Assign an Elastic IP address to each instance that the Site-to-Site VPN must reach
Create a second Site-to-Site VPN connection to the same virtual private gateway
Enable route propagation for the Site-to-Site VPN virtual private gateway in the subnets' route table
explanation: The subnet route table needs routes to the on-premises network that point to the virtual private gateway. Enabling route propagation adds the Site-to-Site VPN routes to the route table automatically while the connection is UP; otherwise the routes must be entered by hand.

choiceExplanations.0: Traffic from a Site-to-Site VPN connection reaches the VPC through the virtual private gateway and the route table entries that point to it, not through an internet gateway.
choiceExplanations.1: The routes to the on-premises network point at the virtual private gateway, so the private subnets are reached through those routes; public IP addresses on the instances are not part of that path.
choiceExplanations.2: The tunnels are already UP, so a second connection would not add the missing routes to the subnets' route table.

resources.title: (Virtual private gateway) Enable route propagation in your route table

question:
A retail chain has branch offices in several cities. Each branch has an internet connection and a router that supports BGP, and the branch IP ranges do not overlap. The branches must exchange data with one another and with one VPC. Management wants the lowest-cost option and no new physical circuits.
Which solution should the company use?
choices: A new Direct Connect connection from every branch office to a Direct Connect gateway attached to the VPC
A dynamically routed Site-to-Site VPN connection from each branch to one shared virtual private gateway (VPN CloudHub)
An AWS Client VPN endpoint in the VPC, with the router at each branch office connecting as a VPN client
VPC peering connections between the VPC and the network of each branch office, with route table entries
explanation: AWS VPN CloudHub connects several Site-to-Site VPN connections to a single virtual private gateway with dynamic routing, so branches can reach each other and the VPC. It suits branch offices that already have internet connections, as a potentially low-cost hub-and-spoke model.

choiceExplanations.0: Direct Connect needs a physical connection from every site to a Direct Connect location, which means new circuits and a higher cost.
choiceExplanations.2: Client VPN is a client-based VPN for individual users with OpenVPN-based clients; it is not meant to join branch networks.
choiceExplanations.3: A VPC peering connection is a networking connection between two VPCs, so it cannot connect an on-premises branch network.

resources.title: Secure communication between AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections using VPN CloudHub

question:
A manufacturer's plant in Singapore reaches workloads in us-east-1 through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the internet, and users complain that performance is unstable because of internet routing. The company wants better network performance, must keep using Site-to-Site VPN, and can use a transit gateway.
Which option should the company choose?
choices: Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection attached to a transit gateway, with acceleration enabled
Turn on acceleration for a Site-to-Site VPN connection that is attached to a virtual private gateway
Enable ECMP across several Site-to-Site VPN connections attached to a transit gateway
Add a second Site-to-Site VPN connection to the same virtual private gateway for redundancy
explanation: An accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection uses AWS Global Accelerator to send traffic to the nearest AWS edge location and over the AWS global network, avoiding disruptions on the public internet. Acceleration is supported only for connections attached to a transit gateway and must be chosen when the connection is created.

choiceExplanations.1: Acceleration is not supported on a virtual private gateway; it works only for connections attached to a transit gateway.
choiceExplanations.2: ECMP aggregates several VPN tunnels to get more bandwidth; it does not move the traffic off the public internet path.
choiceExplanations.3: A second standard connection still runs over the internet, so it does not remove the internet routing that causes the unstable performance.

question:
Remote employees must reach EC2 instances in private subnets and a small on-premises network from their laptops. Each employee must sign in through the company's SAML 2.0 identity provider, and the company does not want to run or patch VPN servers.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Client VPN
AWS Transit Gateway
explanation: AWS Client VPN is a managed client-based VPN that gives users access to AWS and on-premises resources from OpenVPN-based clients. It supports SAML-based federated authentication and removes the work of running VPN servers.

choiceExplanations.0: Site-to-Site VPN connects a customer gateway device at a site to AWS; it is not a service that individual employees sign in to from laptops.
choiceExplanations.1: Direct Connect is a dedicated physical connection between a network and AWS, not an access method for individual laptops.
choiceExplanations.3: A transit gateway is a network transit hub that interconnects VPCs and on-premises networks; it does not provide user sign-in for laptops.

resources.title: Client authentication in AWS Client VPN

question:
Remote employees connect to a VPC through an AWS Client VPN endpoint. All of their traffic, including video calls and web browsing, goes through the tunnel, which raises outbound data transfer from AWS. The company wants only traffic for the VPC to use the tunnel.
Which Client VPN option should the company enable?
choices: Client VPN split-tunnel mode
Client VPN authorization rules
Client VPN connection logging
Client VPN mutual authentication
explanation: With split-tunnel enabled, only traffic destined for networks in the Client VPN endpoint's route table goes over the tunnel. This reduces the outgoing traffic from AWS and so the data transfer cost.

choiceExplanations.1: Authorization rules act as firewall rules that grant clients access to networks; they do not decide which client traffic is sent through the tunnel.
choiceExplanations.2: Connection logging gives visibility into client connections; it does not change how client traffic is routed.
choiceExplanations.3: Mutual authentication uses client certificates to authenticate clients; it does not change routing.

resources.title: Split-tunnel on AWS Client VPN endpoints

question:
The security team at a software company must give 60 remote developers access to private subnets from their laptops. Development and production are separate subnet ranges in one VPC. Developers are in AWS Managed Microsoft AD groups: every developer may reach development, but only the release engineers may reach production. The team wants the LEAST operational overhead and no VPN servers to patch.
Which solution should the team implement?
choices: A self-managed OpenVPN server on Amazon EC2 in an Auto Scaling group, with security groups that limit each developer group
AWS Client VPN with Active Directory authentication, and an authorization rule for each AD group and subnet range
AWS Site-to-Site VPN, with a customer gateway device configured on each developer's laptop
AWS Direct Connect with a private virtual interface from each developer's home network
explanation: Client VPN is managed, supports Active Directory authentication, and lets you configure network-based access rules at the AD group level. An authorization rule per group and destination range limits who can reach development and production.

choiceExplanations.0: A self-managed OpenVPN server works, but the company would deploy and maintain it, which Client VPN removes as a managed service.
choiceExplanations.2: Site-to-Site VPN joins a network through a customer gateway device and is not a client-based VPN for individual laptops.
choiceExplanations.3: Direct Connect needs a physical connection at a Direct Connect location; it is not a way to connect individual home networks.

question:
As the solutions architect, you manage an AWS Client VPN endpoint associated with one subnet of a VPC. Remote users can already reach instances in the VPC. The VPC is joined to the company's on-premises network, 172.16.0.0/16, by an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection, and the users must now reach servers in that network too.
Which TWO actions should you take? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Add a route for 172.16.0.0/16 to the Client VPN endpoint route table, with the associated subnet as the target
Enable split-tunnel on the Client VPN endpoint so that it advertises the on-premises network to the clients
Add an authorization rule on the Client VPN endpoint that lets the users' group reach 172.16.0.0/16
Associate the Client VPN endpoint's target network with the virtual private gateway of the Site-to-Site VPN connection
Attach an internet gateway to the VPC so that Client VPN traffic can reach the on-premises network
explanation: To give Client VPN users access to an on-premises network that is reachable from the VPC, the endpoint needs a route to the on-premises CIDR whose target is the associated subnet, and an authorization rule that lets the clients reach that CIDR.

choiceExplanations.1: Split-tunnel only controls which of the endpoint's routes are pushed to clients; it does not create the missing route or the authorization.
choiceExplanations.3: A target network is a VPC subnet or a transit gateway; the route to the on-premises CIDR is what directs traffic toward the Site-to-Site VPN connection.
choiceExplanations.4: The documented setup uses the existing Site-to-Site VPN (or Direct Connect) link between the VPC and the on-premises network, not an internet gateway.

question:
A software vendor wants hundreds of customers, each with its own AWS account and VPC, to use its service privately from their VPCs. Many customer VPCs use the same IP address ranges, and the vendor does not want any traffic to cross the internet.
Which AWS service should the vendor use?
choices: AWS Transit Gateway
VPC peering
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
AWS PrivateLink
explanation: AWS PrivateLink lets consumers reach a provider's endpoint service through interface endpoints in their own VPCs with private IP addresses. It is a good fit when the VPCs have overlapping IP addresses.

choiceExplanations.0: A transit gateway cannot attach two VPCs that have the same CIDR, so overlapping customer VPCs cannot be joined to it.
choiceExplanations.1: VPC peering needs non-overlapping CIDR ranges between the peered VPCs.
choiceExplanations.2: Site-to-Site VPN connects an on-premises network to a VPC, and it also recommends non-overlapping CIDR blocks; it is not a way to publish a service to many VPCs.

question:
A data center connected to a VPC by AWS Direct Connect must read objects from Amazon S3 without using the public internet. The team created a gateway endpoint for S3 in the VPC, but the on-premises servers still cannot use it.
Which VPC endpoint should the team create?
choices: A PrivateLink Gateway Load Balancer endpoint in the VPC
A PrivateLink interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC
A second S3 gateway endpoint with a more permissive endpoint policy
A NAT gateway in a public subnet, with S3 traffic routed to it
explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 do not allow access from on premises, while interface endpoints (powered by AWS PrivateLink) use private IP addresses in the VPC and are reachable from on premises over Direct Connect or VPN.

choiceExplanations.0: A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint sends traffic to a fleet of virtual appliances; it is not an entry point for Amazon S3.
choiceExplanations.2: An endpoint policy controls which principals can use an endpoint; it does not make a gateway endpoint reachable from on premises.
choiceExplanations.3: A NAT device lets instances in private subnets reach Amazon S3 through the internet gateway; it is not an entry point for on-premises servers.

question:
A security vendor runs a fleet of traffic-inspection appliances in its own VPC and sells inspection as a service. Customers in other AWS accounts must send their VPC traffic through the appliances transparently, by adding routes to their own route tables, without gaining network access to anything else in the vendor's VPC. The appliance fleet must scale with demand.
Which design should the vendor use?
choices: An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service backed by a Gateway Load Balancer, with customers routing traffic to Gateway Load Balancer endpoints
An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer, with customers calling the endpoint's DNS name from their applications
VPC peering between each customer VPC and the vendor VPC, with routes in both VPCs that point to the appliances
A public Network Load Balancer in front of the appliances, with customer route tables pointing to its public IP addresses
explanation: A Gateway Load Balancer endpoint service is accessed through Gateway Load Balancer endpoints that customers add as route table targets. The load balancer distributes traffic to the appliances and scales with demand, and customers reach only the endpoint service.

choiceExplanations.1: An interface endpoint sends TCP or UDP traffic to an endpoint service that is resolved by DNS, so applications must be changed; it does not steer a VPC's traffic through route tables.
choiceExplanations.2: A VPC peering connection is a networking connection between two VPCs, which gives the customers network access to the vendor's VPC.
choiceExplanations.3: Route tables for this pattern target Gateway Load Balancer endpoints, which a public Network Load Balancer does not provide; it would also expose the appliances on public addresses.

resources.title: Access virtual appliances through AWS PrivateLink

question:
A team wants instances in private subnets to keep calling the default public Amazon SQS endpoint name, but with the requests resolved to private IP addresses through an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint with private DNS names enabled.
Which TWO VPC settings must be turned on for this to work? (Choose TWO.)
choices: A route to the AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint in every subnet route table
An internet gateway attached to the VPC that holds the AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint
DNS hostnames turned on for the VPC that holds the AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint
A gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS created next to the AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint
DNS resolution turned on for the VPC that holds the AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint
explanation: Private DNS names for an interface endpoint work when the VPC has both DNS hostnames and DNS resolution enabled; AWS then creates a hidden private hosted zone that resolves the public service name to the endpoint network interfaces.

choiceExplanations.0: Traffic to an interface endpoint is resolved by DNS to the private IP addresses of its network interfaces; route table entries are used by gateway endpoints.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS PrivateLink connects a VPC to the service without an internet gateway.
choiceExplanations.3: Gateway endpoints exist only for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, so there is no gateway endpoint for Amazon SQS.

resources.title: Access AWS services through AWS PrivateLink

question:
A company is building a chat feature. Browsers need a persistent, two-way connection to AWS Lambda functions that process each message, and the company does not want to manage any servers.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: Amazon SQS
AWS Step Functions
Amazon Route 53
Amazon API Gateway
explanation: Amazon API Gateway can create WebSocket APIs, which support two-way communication between clients and a backend such as AWS Lambda, without servers to manage.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon SQS is a hosted queue that decouples components; it does not keep a two-way connection open to browsers.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Step Functions builds workflows of steps that call other AWS services; it does not accept browser connections.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon Route 53 is a DNS service that routes traffic to resources; it does not keep a connection open between browsers and Lambda.

resources.title: Overview of WebSocket APIs in API Gateway

question:
A company sells access to its API Gateway REST API to external developers. Free-tier customers must be throttled to a lower request rate and a smaller monthly quota than paid customers.
Which API Gateway feature should the company use?
choices: API Gateway stage caching
API Gateway canary release deployments
API Gateway usage plans with API keys
API Gateway Lambda authorizers
explanation: A usage plan specifies who can access the deployed API stages and methods through API keys, and sets throttling and quota limits per key. Separate plans can give free and paid customers different limits.

choiceExplanations.0: Stage caching stores endpoint responses to reduce calls to the backend; it does not set per-customer limits.
choiceExplanations.1: A canary release deployment is a way to roll out changes safely; it does not limit customers' request rates.
choiceExplanations.3: A Lambda authorizer is an authentication mechanism that decides whether a caller is allowed; it does not set per-customer throttling and quotas.

resources.title: Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway

question: An application uses Amazon API Gateway to front AWS Lambda functions that hold payroll data. Only internal services running in three VPCs may call the API, and the security team requires that the API not be reachable from the internet. As the solutions architect, which API Gateway configuration meets these requirements?
choices: A Regional API Gateway REST API, with a resource policy that allows only the NAT gateway Elastic IP addresses of the three VPCs
An API Gateway private REST API invoked through interface VPC endpoints, with a resource policy that allows only the approved VPC endpoints
An edge-optimized API Gateway REST API, with AWS IAM authorization turned on for every method of the API
An API Gateway HTTP API with a custom domain name, protected by a JWT authorizer
explanation: A private API is a REST API that can be called only from within a VPC, through an interface VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink. A resource policy that uses the aws:SourceVpce or aws:SourceVpc condition limits it to the approved endpoints or VPCs.

choiceExplanations.0: Only a private API is limited to callers inside a VPC; a Regional endpoint with an IP-based resource policy is still not a private API.
choiceExplanations.2: An edge-optimized endpoint is served through a CloudFront distribution to reach clients, and IAM authorization controls who may call but does not make the API private.
choiceExplanations.3: An HTTP API cannot be private, because private APIs support only REST APIs; a JWT authorizer controls who may call but does not make the API private.

resources.title: Private REST APIs in API Gateway

question:
A mobile app sends orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The team wants each order buffered in an Amazon SQS standard queue for later processing, and it does not want to write or run any code between API Gateway and the queue.
Which API Gateway configuration meets this requirement?
choices: A Lambda proxy integration that points straight at the SQS queue
An HTTP proxy integration that forwards each request to the SQS queue URL unchanged
An AWS service integration that calls the SQS SendMessage action, using an IAM role for API Gateway
A mock integration that returns a success response and then forwards the request body to the queue
explanation: An AWS service integration lets an API expose an AWS service action. API Gateway can call SQS SendMessage directly with the right integration request and an IAM role, so no Lambda function or other code is needed.

choiceExplanations.0: The Lambda proxy integration is for invoking a Lambda function and does not apply to other AWS service actions.
choiceExplanations.1: An HTTP proxy integration is for backend HTTP endpoints; for an AWS service action the AWS integration type is used.
choiceExplanations.3: A mock integration makes API Gateway answer the request itself without sending it to a backend, so nothing reaches the queue.

resources.title: Choose an API Gateway API integration type

question:
A central networking account owns a VPC and its subnets. Application teams in other accounts of the same AWS Organization must launch their own EC2 instances into those subnets, and the company does not want to build a separate VPC in each account.
Which AWS service lets the networking account share the subnets?
choices: AWS RAM
AWS PrivateLink
AWS Transit Gateway
AWS Organizations service control policies
explanation: VPC subnet sharing uses AWS RAM: the owner shares subnets, and participant accounts in the organization can create their own resources, such as EC2 instances, in the shared subnets.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS PrivateLink gives a VPC private access to services and resources; it does not place other accounts' instances in a subnet.
choiceExplanations.2: A transit gateway interconnects VPCs and on-premises networks, so each account would still need its own VPC.
choiceExplanations.3: Service control policies set permission guardrails and grant no permissions, so they cannot share a subnet.

resources.title: Share your VPC subnets with other accounts

question:
A networking team uses AWS RAM to share a transit gateway with the Workloads OU of its AWS Organization. New accounts join that OU every month and must get access automatically, without any action by the networking team. Accounts in other OUs must not get access.
How should the team create the resource share?
choices: Add every current account ID in the OU as a principal of the AWS RAM resource share
Add the whole organization as the principal of the AWS RAM resource share
Add the management account as the only principal of the AWS RAM resource share
Add the Workloads OU as the principal of the AWS RAM resource share
explanation: AWS RAM can share with an OU instead of enumerating accounts. When an account is added to an OU that has access to a resource share, the new member account automatically gets access.

choiceExplanations.0: Listing account IDs means enumerating each account, so every new account would need the share to be updated.
choiceExplanations.1: Sharing with the whole organization gives every account in every OU access, including the OUs that must be excluded.
choiceExplanations.2: Sharing only with the management account does not give the member accounts in the OU access.

resources.title: What is AWS Resource Access Manager?

question: A company's network account owns a transit gateway in eu-west-1. Forty other accounts in the same organization must attach their own VPCs to it, and new accounts will join over time. The company wants a single transit gateway whose route tables stay under the network team's control, and the LEAST ongoing administration. As the solutions architect, how should you provide this?
choices: Create a transit gateway in each account and connect them with transit gateway peering attachments
Share the transit gateway with the organization by using AWS RAM, and have each account create its own VPC attachment
Peer every VPC with a hub VPC in the network account, and route all traffic through the hub VPC
Publish the transit gateway to the other accounts as an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service
explanation: A transit gateway can be shared with an organization by using AWS RAM. Accounts it is shared with can create VPC attachments in their own VPCs, but they cannot create, modify or delete its route tables, so the network team keeps control.

choiceExplanations.0: This creates a transit gateway in every account instead of one, and each would need its own peering attachments and route tables.
choiceExplanations.2: VPC peering is non-transitive, so traffic cannot be routed through a hub VPC to other VPCs.
choiceExplanations.3: An endpoint service must be backed by a load balancer, so a transit gateway cannot be published as one.

question:
A security architect reviews how a company shares resources with AWS RAM, both across its AWS Organization and with a partner's account that is outside the organization.
Which TWO statements about AWS RAM are correct? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Accounts inside the organization must accept an invitation even after sharing with AWS Organizations is enabled in AWS RAM
A partner account outside the organization gets access to an AWS RAM resource share only after it accepts an invitation
An AWS RAM resource share can include Regional resources from any Region where the owner has resources
Principals use a shared Regional resource in the Region where it was created, because AWS RAM is a Regional service
AWS RAM copies each shared resource into every account that the resource share includes
explanation: Accounts outside the organization receive an invitation and get access only after they accept it, while accounts inside the organization need none once sharing with AWS Organizations is enabled. AWS RAM is a Regional service, so principals use a shared Regional resource in the Region where it was created.

choiceExplanations.0: After you enable sharing with AWS Organizations, AWS RAM does not send invitations to principals in your organization.
choiceExplanations.2: A resource share can contain only Regional resources that are in the same Region as the resource share.
choiceExplanations.4: The owning account keeps ownership of a shared resource and no duplicate resources are created in the other accounts.

resources.title: What is AWS Resource Access Manager?

question:
A logistics company's suppliers upload files with FTPS clients. The files must land in an Amazon EFS file system that Linux application servers mount, and the company does not want to run or patch FTP servers.
Which AWS service should it use?
choices: AWS DataSync
Amazon AppFlow
AWS Storage Gateway
AWS Transfer Family
explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides managed servers for SFTP, FTPS and FTP that transfer files into and out of Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS, without any server infrastructure to run.

choiceExplanations.0: DataSync transfers data between storage systems and AWS storage services; it does not offer FTPS server endpoints for suppliers' clients.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon AppFlow exchanges data between SaaS applications and AWS services; it is not a file transfer server for FTPS clients.
choiceExplanations.2: A Storage Gateway file gateway gives on-premises applications NFS or SMB access to Amazon S3; it is not an FTPS server in front of Amazon EFS.

question:
A company runs an AWS Transfer Family SFTP server. Partner employees must sign in with the passwords of their existing accounts in AWS Managed Microsoft AD, and the company wants the LEAST operational overhead and no custom code.
Which identity provider option should the company choose for the server?
choices: Transfer Family service-managed users with SSH keys
Transfer Family with a custom identity provider built on AWS Lambda
Transfer Family with AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity provider
Transfer Family with a custom identity provider built on Amazon API Gateway
explanation: Transfer Family can use AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity provider, and it supports password authentication for SFTP, FTPS and FTP with no custom code.

choiceExplanations.0: Service-managed users on an SFTP server authenticate with keys and do not support passwords.
choiceExplanations.1: A custom identity provider on AWS Lambda works with passwords but the company would have to build and maintain the function, which the requirement rules out.
choiceExplanations.3: A custom identity provider on Amazon API Gateway requires you to provide the API and an IAM role to integrate the directory, which is custom work.

resources.title: Configuring an SFTP, FTPS, or FTP server endpoint

question:
An insurance broker network sends claim files to a company's on-premises SFTP server. Hundreds of brokers have scripts that use the hostname claims.example.com and sign in with SSH keys. The company is retiring the server and wants the files in Amazon S3, with every uploaded file tagged and copied to an archive prefix automatically, no servers to run, and no change to the broker scripts.
Which solution should the company implement?
choices: An AWS Transfer Family SFTP server with the custom hostname claims.example.com and a managed workflow that tags and copies each upload
An SFTP server on an Amazon EC2 instance, with a cron job that tags and copies new files to Amazon S3
An Amazon S3 bucket with an event notification, and presigned URLs sent to each broker for uploads
An AWS Storage Gateway file gateway, with each broker mounting its share over NFS or SMB
explanation: Transfer Family servers keep clients' existing configuration, support a custom hostname through Route 53 or another DNS provider, and can authenticate with keys. Managed workflows run steps such as tagging and copying after a file is uploaded.

choiceExplanations.1: An EC2 instance is a server the company would run, patch and script, which the requirements rule out.
choiceExplanations.2: Presigned URLs are not SFTP, so every broker script would have to change.
choiceExplanations.3: A file gateway exposes NFS and SMB file shares rather than SFTP, so every broker script would have to change.

question:
Business partners send purchase orders to a company with FTPS clients over the internet. Each partner's firewall allows outbound connections only to a short list of fixed IP addresses that the company must supply. The files go to Amazon S3, and the company wants to run no servers.
Which Transfer Family server endpoint configuration meets these requirements?
choices: A Transfer Family server with a public endpoint and the FTPS protocol
A Transfer Family server with a VPC hosted endpoint that has internal access
A Transfer Family server with an internet-facing VPC hosted endpoint and plain FTP
A Transfer Family server with an internet-facing VPC hosted endpoint and Elastic IP addresses
explanation: An internet-facing VPC hosted endpoint supports SFTP and FTPS and can have Elastic IP addresses attached, which do not change, so partners can allow-list them in their firewalls.

choiceExplanations.0: A public endpoint supports only SFTP, and AWS-provided IP addresses subject to change cannot be attached as static addresses.
choiceExplanations.1: An endpoint with internal access is reachable only from within the VPC and VPC-connected environments, not by partners over the internet.
choiceExplanations.2: Only SFTP and FTPS can be used on an internet-facing VPC hosted endpoint, and plain FTP is not supported there.

resources.title: Configuring an SFTP, FTPS, or FTP server endpoint
Create a server in a virtual private cloud

question: A startup serves a public web application from EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. It has no budget for paid security subscriptions but wants automatic protection against network and transport layer DDoS attacks such as TCP SYN floods. Which service provides this at no extra charge?
choices: AWS Shield Advanced
AWS Shield Standard
AWS WAF
Amazon GuardDuty
explanation: AWS Shield Standard is applied automatically for every AWS customer at no additional charge. It defends against the most common network and transport layer DDoS attacks, such as TCP SYN floods.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS Shield Advanced is an optional subscription for higher levels of protection, so it does not fit a company that has no budget for paid security subscriptions.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS WAF filters HTTP(S) requests at the application layer, and it is billed per web ACL, per rule and per million requests inspected, so it is neither free nor a network layer DDoS defense.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes logs and other data sources for suspicious activity; it is not a DDoS protection service.

resources.title: How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work

question: AWS Shield Advanced protects several CloudFront distributions and Application Load Balancers that together serve one application. The security team wants attacks on them detected and mitigated as a single unit, with newly protected resources joining automatically. Which Shield Advanced feature should it use?
choices: Shield Advanced proactive engagement
Shield Advanced cost protection
Shield Advanced protection groups
Shield Advanced health-based detection
explanation: Protection groups let you treat several protected resources as a single unit for detection and mitigation. Newly protected resources that match the group's criteria are included automatically.

choiceExplanations.0: Proactive engagement lets the Shield Response Team contact you directly when the Route 53 health check of a protected resource becomes unhealthy during an event; it does not group resources.
choiceExplanations.1: Cost protection offers Shield Advanced service credits for bill spikes caused by a DDoS attack on protected resources; it does not change how attacks are detected.
choiceExplanations.3: Health-based detection uses Route 53 health checks to make detection of a protected resource more accurate and faster; it does not combine several resources into one unit.

resources.title: Grouping your AWS Shield Advanced protections
AWS Shield Advanced capabilities and options
