explanation: In Distributed mode a Map state can read a CSV file straight from Amazon S3 and run up to 10,000 parallel child workflow executions, each with its own execution history. That removes the input size and history limits of Inline mode.

choiceExplanations.0: A Parallel state runs the branches that are written into the workflow definition, so it cannot create one branch for each of millions of rows.
choiceExplanations.1: Inline mode accepts only a JSON array as input, limits the payload to 256 KiB, supports up to 40 concurrent iterations and adds every iteration to the parent's execution history.
choiceExplanations.3: A looping Choice state would process the rows one after another instead of in parallel.

question:
A retailer wants Salesforce account data copied into Amazon Redshift every night, without anyone writing integration code. The security team requires that the data transfer does not travel over the public internet.
Which AWS service should the retailer use?
choices: AWS DataSync
AWS Database Migration Service
Amazon AppFlow
AWS Transfer Family
explanation: Amazon AppFlow transfers data between SaaS applications such as Salesforce and AWS services such as Amazon Redshift without code. Its private flows use AWS PrivateLink, so the data moves over AWS infrastructure instead of the public internet.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DataSync transfers file and object data between storage systems. It does not pull records from a SaaS application such as Salesforce.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS DMS migrates and replicates data stores such as databases. Salesforce is a SaaS application, not one of the data stores it migrates.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Transfer Family provides SFTP, FTPS and FTP file transfers into and out of AWS storage. It does not copy records out of Salesforce.

question:
A support team uses Amazon AppFlow to copy Salesforce records into Amazon S3 for analysis. The flow must run as soon as a record changes in Salesforce, rather than at a fixed time or when someone starts it.
Which AppFlow flow trigger meets this requirement?
choices: An AppFlow flow with the run-on-event trigger
An AppFlow flow with the run-on-demand trigger
An AppFlow flow with the run-on-schedule trigger and full transfer
An AppFlow flow with the run-on-schedule trigger and incremental transfer
explanation: An event-triggered flow runs in response to a change event in the source SaaS application, so the flow starts when the Salesforce record changes.

choiceExplanations.1: On-demand flows run only when a user starts them manually.
choiceExplanations.2: Schedule-triggered flows run on the recurring schedule you set, not when a change happens. Full transfer also copies a snapshot of all records on each run.
choiceExplanations.3: Incremental transfer only limits what a scheduled run copies. The run still starts on the schedule instead of when the record changes.

question:
A marketing analytics group needs Zendesk support tickets in Amazon S3 as Parquet files, partitioned for fast queries, with the tables registered automatically so analysts can query them in Amazon Athena. The group has no developers and wants the LEAST operational overhead.
Which solution should it choose?
choices: An AWS Database Migration Service task that replicates the tickets to Amazon S3, with an AWS Glue crawler to register the files
An AWS DataSync task that copies the tickets to Amazon S3 on a schedule, with an AWS Glue crawler to register the files
An AWS Lambda function on an Amazon EventBridge schedule that calls the Zendesk API and writes the files to Amazon S3
An Amazon AppFlow flow to Amazon S3 that writes Parquet, partitions the output and catalogs it in the AWS Glue Data Catalog
explanation: Amazon AppFlow can transfer Zendesk data to Amazon S3 without code. Its S3 destination settings include Parquet output, partitioning and cataloging in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, which analytics services such as Athena can use, and no crawler is needed.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DMS migrates and replicates data stores such as databases. Zendesk is a SaaS application, and the crawler adds one more component to run.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS DataSync transfers file and object data between storage systems. It does not connect to a SaaS application such as Zendesk.
choiceExplanations.2: A Lambda function that calls the Zendesk API is custom code that developers must write and maintain, and this group has none.

resources.title: Cataloging the data output from an Amazon AppFlow flow

question: A travel agency's Amazon AppFlow flow must pull Salesforce opportunities every hour. After the first run, each run should transfer only the records added or changed since the last successful run, to keep data volumes low. (Choose TWO.)
choices: Use an AppFlow flow with the run-on-demand trigger and have an analyst start it each hour
Use an AppFlow flow with the run-on-schedule trigger set to hourly
Select full transfer in the AppFlow flow and remove duplicates later with Amazon Athena
Use an AppFlow flow with the run-on-event trigger and choose incremental transfer
Select incremental transfer in the AppFlow flow
explanation: A schedule-triggered flow runs on the hourly schedule, and for schedule-triggered flows you can select incremental transfer. Each run then copies only the records added or changed since the last successful run.

choiceExplanations.0: On-demand flows run only when a user starts them, so the hourly pull would depend on a person.
choiceExplanations.2: Full transfer copies a snapshot of all records on every run, which keeps data volumes high.
choiceExplanations.3: Event-triggered flows start when the source application reports a change event, not on an hourly schedule, and the full or incremental choice applies to schedule-triggered flows.

question:
A company's on-premises order system exchanges messages through queues and topics by using the OpenWire and STOMP protocols. The company is moving to AWS and wants neither to rewrite the messaging code nor to manage broker servers.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: Amazon SQS
Amazon SNS
Amazon MQ
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
explanation: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ. ActiveMQ brokers support wire-level protocols such as OpenWire and STOMP, so existing applications can move without rewriting their messaging code.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon SQS is a cloud-native queue service with its own API, so an application that speaks OpenWire or STOMP would have to be rewritten.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon SNS is a cloud-native publish/subscribe service with its own API, so an application that speaks OpenWire or STOMP would have to be rewritten.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is a streaming data service, not a message broker with queues and topics that speaks OpenWire or STOMP.

question:
A company runs an Apache ActiveMQ broker on Amazon MQ, and its applications connect with the OpenWire protocol. The broker is in one Availability Zone, and the applications must keep working automatically if that zone fails.
Which Amazon MQ configuration meets this requirement?
choices: An Amazon MQ single-instance broker with a larger broker instance type
An Amazon MQ active/standby broker across two Availability Zones
An Amazon MQ single-instance broker that uses Amazon EBS storage
An Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ cluster deployment across three Availability Zones
explanation: An active/standby broker is a pair of brokers in two Availability Zones that share Amazon EFS storage. If the active broker fails, the standby takes over, and the ActiveMQ clients keep using their wire-level protocol.

choiceExplanations.0: A single-instance broker runs in one Availability Zone, so a larger instance type does not protect against that zone failing.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon EBS storage replicates data only within a single Availability Zone, and the broker is still one instance in one zone.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ is a different engine that is accessed over AMQP 0-9-1, so the OpenWire clients could not connect to it.

resources.title: Deployment options for Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ brokers

question:
A logistics firm runs RabbitMQ on premises, and its services connect with AMQP 0-9-1 client libraries. During the move to AWS the firm wants to keep that client code, survive the loss of an Availability Zone and stop managing broker servers.
Which solution should the firm choose?
choices: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ with a single-instance broker in one Availability Zone
Amazon SQS FIFO queues, with the services changed to use the Amazon SQS API
Amazon MSK with brokers in three Availability Zones, with the services changed to use Kafka clients
Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ with a cluster deployment across multiple Availability Zones
explanation: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ is managed and is accessed over AMQP 0-9-1, so the client code stays. A cluster deployment runs three broker nodes across multiple Availability Zones with classic mirroring, so the loss of one zone does not stop the broker.

choiceExplanations.0: A single-instance broker runs in one Availability Zone, so an outage of that zone stops the broker.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon SQS has its own API, so the services would have to be rewritten instead of keeping their AMQP client code.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon MSK is managed Apache Kafka, which uses Kafka clients, so the services would have to be rewritten instead of keeping their AMQP client code.

resources.title: Deployment options for Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ brokers

question:
A food-delivery platform stores high volumes of persistent order messages in an ActiveMQ broker on Amazon MQ. It needs the best throughput and lowest latency that persistent storage allows, and a broker in a single Availability Zone is acceptable because the team can recreate it after an outage.
Which TWO actions should the team take? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Create an Amazon MQ active/standby broker
Choose Amazon EFS as the storage type of the Amazon MQ broker
Create an Amazon MQ single-instance broker
Choose Amazon EBS as the storage type of the Amazon MQ broker
Turn on cross-Region data replication for the Amazon MQ broker
explanation: For ActiveMQ brokers, Amazon EBS is the storage option for low latency and high throughput, while Amazon EFS is the option for durability across Availability Zones. EBS replicates data within one zone and does not support active/standby, so it is used with a single-instance broker.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon EBS does not support the active/standby deployment mode, so an active/standby broker would have to use Amazon EFS, the durability option rather than the throughput option.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon EFS replicates data across Availability Zones for durability. It is the durability option, not the low-latency, high-throughput option.
choiceExplanations.4: Cross-Region data replication copies messages to a broker in another Region for recovery. It does not improve throughput or latency.

resources.title: Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ storage types

question:
A company's developers already write stream-processing applications with the Apache Kafka producer and consumer APIs. They want a fully managed service in their VPC that runs those applications unchanged and removes broker and ZooKeeper maintenance.
Which AWS service should they use?
choices: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon MSK
Amazon SQS
Amazon Data Firehose
explanation: Amazon MSK runs open-source Apache Kafka as a fully managed service, so existing Kafka applications and tools work without code changes. MSK creates and manages the Kafka brokers and ZooKeeper nodes.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams has its own API, so applications written for the Kafka APIs would have to be rewritten.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon SQS is a message queue service with its own API. It is not a Kafka-compatible service.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Data Firehose delivers streaming data to destinations. It is not a Kafka platform that producers and consumers connect to.

resources.title: Welcome to the Amazon MSK Developer Guide

question:
A startup streams application events through Amazon MSK. Traffic is spiky and hard to predict, and the small team does not want to choose broker sizes or scale cluster capacity itself.
Which MSK option fits best?
choices: MSK Serverless clusters
MSK Provisioned clusters with Standard brokers
MSK Replicator between two clusters
MSK Connect with an autoscaled connector
explanation: MSK Serverless runs Apache Kafka without capacity management. It automatically provisions and scales capacity, so the team does not right-size or scale a cluster.

choiceExplanations.1: With a provisioned cluster you choose the broker type and the number of brokers, so you still plan the cluster capacity.
choiceExplanations.2: MSK Replicator copies data between MSK clusters. It does not remove the need to size the clusters.
choiceExplanations.3: MSK Connect runs Kafka Connect connectors that move data into and out of Kafka. It does not provide the Kafka cluster capacity.

question:
A bank's change-data-capture pipeline uses the Debezium connector on Kafka Connect to stream database changes into Kafka topics, and an Amazon S3 sink connector to land them in a data lake. The bank is moving to AWS and wants to reuse the connector configurations unchanged, with no Kafka Connect servers to patch or scale.
Which solution is the best fit?
choices: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, with the database changes written through the Kinesis Producer Library
Amazon MSK with MSK Connect running the Debezium and Amazon S3 sink connectors
Amazon MSK with Kafka Connect workers that the bank runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group
AWS DMS replicating the database changes to Amazon S3, with the connector settings rebuilt as DMS task settings
explanation: MSK Connect runs Kafka Connect connectors as a managed capability. You can deploy third-party connectors such as Debezium, or an existing connector with no code changes, and MSK Connect patches, manages and autoscales the underlying infrastructure.

choiceExplanations.0: Kinesis Data Streams is not Kafka, so the Debezium and Kafka Connect connector configurations could not be reused.
choiceExplanations.2: Running Kafka Connect workers on EC2 instances leaves the bank patching and scaling servers, which the requirements rule out.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS DMS is a replication service with its own tasks and settings, so the bank would rebuild the pipeline instead of reusing its connector configurations.

question:
A security team requires that the Lambda functions and EC2 clients that use an Amazon MSK cluster authenticate with their IAM roles, that topic permissions be written in IAM policies, and that nobody creates or rotates passwords or client certificates.
Which MSK feature should the team enable?
choices: MSK SASL/SCRAM authentication with credentials kept in AWS Secrets Manager
MSK mutual TLS authentication with certificates from AWS Private CA
MSK unauthenticated access that is limited by security group rules
MSK IAM access control for both authentication and authorization
explanation: IAM access control for Amazon MSK handles both authentication and authorization with IAM identities and policies. Clients use their IAM roles, so there are no passwords or client certificates to create or rotate.

choiceExplanations.0: SASL/SCRAM uses sign-in credentials stored in Secrets Manager, which are passwords that must be created and rotated, and Kafka ACLs handle the authorization.
choiceExplanations.1: Mutual TLS needs client certificates issued by a private CA, and access to topics is controlled with Kafka ACLs rather than IAM policies.
choiceExplanations.2: Unauthenticated access does not identify clients by their IAM role, so topic permissions cannot be written in IAM policies.

resources.title: Authentication and authorization for Apache Kafka APIs

question:
Business analysts must clean a customer data set in Amazon S3: fix inconsistent date formats, remove null values and standardize product names. They cannot write code and want a visual, point-and-click tool with no servers to manage.
Which AWS service should they use?
choices: Amazon Athena
AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon QuickSight
Amazon EMR
explanation: AWS Glue DataBrew is a serverless visual data preparation tool with more than 250 point-and-click transformations to clean and normalize data without writing code. It saves the prepared data set to Amazon S3.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Athena runs SQL queries on data in Amazon S3. Cleaning data with it means writing SQL.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon QuickSight builds dashboards and business intelligence reports. It is not a tool for cleaning a data set and writing it back to S3.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon EMR runs Hadoop and Spark clusters, so it needs code and cluster setup.

question:
A scheduled AWS Glue ETL job reads new CSV files from Amazon S3 every night. Each run reprocesses all the older files too and creates duplicates in the target. The job should handle only data it has not processed before.
Which Glue feature should the team turn on?
choices: An AWS Glue crawler that runs on a schedule
The AWS Glue Studio visual editor
AWS Glue job bookmarks on the job
AWS Glue DataBrew recipe steps
explanation: A job bookmark makes AWS Glue keep state about what earlier runs processed. A job that runs again on a schedule then processes only new data and avoids duplicate output.

choiceExplanations.0: A crawler scans data stores and updates Data Catalog tables. It does not control which data a job processes.
choiceExplanations.1: Glue Studio is a graphical interface for creating, running and monitoring ETL jobs. It does not track which data was already processed.
choiceExplanations.3: DataBrew recipes are saved data-cleaning steps. They do not track which data a job already processed.

resources.title: Tracking processed data using job bookmarks

question:
An IoT company streams sensor readings into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Its engineers have Spark Structured Streaming code that cleans the records, and the results must be written continuously to Amazon S3. The team does not want to provision or manage any cluster.
Which solution should the company choose?
choices: An Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink application that reads from the data stream
An AWS Glue streaming ETL job that reads from the data stream and runs the Spark code
An Amazon EMR cluster that runs the Spark Structured Streaming application
An Amazon Data Firehose stream that reads from the data stream and delivers to Amazon S3
explanation: AWS Glue streaming ETL jobs are serverless and built on the Apache Spark Structured Streaming engine. They can read from Kinesis Data Streams, clean and transform the records, and load the results into Amazon S3.

choiceExplanations.0: Managed Service for Apache Flink runs Apache Flink applications, so the Spark code would have to be rewritten.
choiceExplanations.2: An EMR cluster is made of EC2 instances that the team creates and sizes, so it means managing a cluster, which the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Data Firehose delivers streaming data to destinations such as S3. It does not run the team's existing Spark code.

resources.title: Streaming ETL jobs in AWS Glue

question:
Several teams publish Avro records to topics on an Amazon MSK cluster that other teams consume. A producer recently released a schema change that broke downstream consumers. The platform team wants a new schema version to be rejected at registration if it is incompatible with earlier versions.
Which AWS Glue capability should the team use?
choices: AWS Glue Schema Registry with a compatibility mode set on the schema
An AWS Glue crawler that infers the schema after the records are stored in Amazon S3
AWS Glue job bookmarks on the jobs that consume the topics
An AWS Glue DataBrew recipe that standardizes the fields after the records arrive
explanation: The AWS Glue Schema Registry lets teams centrally manage and evolve data stream schemas, with integrations for Apache Kafka and Amazon MSK. Each schema has a compatibility rule, and requests to register new schema versions are checked against it before they succeed.

choiceExplanations.1: A crawler infers the schema of data that already exists in a data store. It cannot stop an incompatible schema from being released.
choiceExplanations.2: Job bookmarks track which data a job has already processed. They do not validate schemas.
choiceExplanations.3: A DataBrew recipe changes data after it arrives. It cannot stop an incompatible schema version from being registered.

question:
A company is moving the Hadoop jobs it runs on premises, written with Apache Hive and Pig, to AWS with as few changes as possible. The team wants control over the software on the cluster and wants to use Spot Instances to lower cost.
Which AWS service should it use?
choices: Amazon Athena
Amazon EMR
AWS Glue
Amazon Redshift
explanation: Amazon EMR is a managed cluster platform for big data frameworks such as Hadoop, Hive, Pig and Spark. You choose the applications and software on the cluster, and you can use Spot Instances to reduce cost.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service for data in S3, so it does not give the team a Hadoop cluster whose software it controls.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service. It is not a cluster whose software the team controls, so it does not fit moving Hadoop jobs with few changes.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse for SQL analytics, not a platform for running Hadoop jobs.

question:
A company runs a long-lived Amazon EMR cluster. To save money it wants to add Spot Instances for the peak periods, but losing a Spot Instance must never cause loss of HDFS data or end the cluster.
Which EMR node type should run on Spot Instances?
choices: EMR task nodes
EMR core nodes
The EMR primary node
All EMR node types
explanation: Task nodes run tasks but do not store data in HDFS, so their termination loses no data and has minimal effect on the cluster. Running task nodes on Spot Instances is a common way to add capacity at a low cost.

choiceExplanations.1: Core nodes store data in HDFS, so terminating them risks data loss.
choiceExplanations.2: The primary node controls the cluster, and when it terminates the cluster ends.
choiceExplanations.3: Putting every node type on Spot Instances includes the core and primary nodes, which brings both the data loss risk and the risk of the cluster ending.

resources.title: Configuring Amazon EMR cluster instance types and best practices for Spot instances

question:
A platform team runs its microservices on a shared Amazon EKS cluster. The data science group wants to run Apache Spark jobs on that same cluster's capacity instead of operating separate big data clusters, and wants AWS to build and manage the containers for the Spark applications.
As the solutions architect, which service do you recommend?
choices: Amazon EMR on Amazon EC2, with a dedicated cluster for the Spark jobs
AWS Glue ETL jobs, with the Spark scripts moved to Glue
Amazon Athena with Apache Spark notebooks
Amazon EMR on EKS, with the Spark jobs submitted to the existing cluster
explanation: Amazon EMR on EKS is a deployment option that runs open-source big data frameworks such as Spark on Amazon EKS. EMR builds and manages the containers, and EMR workloads can share an EKS cluster with other applications.

choiceExplanations.0: EMR on EC2 means a separate cluster for the Spark jobs, which is what the group wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service that runs jobs in its own managed environment, not on the company's EKS cluster.
choiceExplanations.2: Athena with Apache Spark is serverless and runs in Athena's own managed environment, not on the company's EKS cluster.

resources.title: What is Amazon EMR on EKS?

question: A retailer's nightly sales aggregation runs on Amazon EMR for about two hours. The input and the results must outlive the cluster, and the retailer wants to pay for cluster instances only while the job runs. (Choose TWO.)
choices: Store the input and output data in Amazon S3 instead of in HDFS on the EMR cluster
Keep the data in HDFS on the EMR core nodes so that later clusters can use it
Configure the EMR cluster to terminate after the last step completes
Keep the EMR cluster running all day with termination protection turned on
Keep the data on the EMR instance store volumes for the fastest access
explanation: Using Amazon S3 as the data layer separates storage from compute and keeps the data after the cluster ends. Terminating the cluster after its last step means the instances are billed only for the time the steps run.

choiceExplanations.1: HDFS is ephemeral storage that is reclaimed when the cluster ends, so later clusters could not use the data.
choiceExplanations.3: A long-running cluster keeps accruing charges until someone shuts it down, so the retailer would pay outside the two-hour job.
choiceExplanations.4: Data on instance store volumes persists only for the life of its EC2 instance, so it would not outlive the cluster.

resources.title: Configuring an Amazon EMR cluster to continue or terminate after step execution
Working with storage and file systems with Amazon EMR

question:
A smart-doorbell maker wants homeowners to watch live video from the doorbell on a phone and talk to visitors, over low-latency peer-to-peer connections, without building or running signaling or relay servers.
Which AWS service should the maker use?
choices: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon Data Firehose
Amazon Kinesis Video Streams
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
explanation: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams includes a fully managed WebRTC capability for live peer-to-peer streaming and two-way audio or video between camera devices and mobile or web players, with no signaling or media relay servers to run.

choiceExplanations.0: Kinesis Data Streams collects and processes data records for custom applications. It is not a WebRTC service for live video with visitors.
choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Data Firehose delivers streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3. It does not provide peer-to-peer video connections.
choiceExplanations.3: Managed Service for Apache Flink processes data streams with Flink applications. It does not connect cameras to phones.

resources.title: What is Amazon Kinesis Video Streams with WebRTC?

question:
Operations staff must watch both live and previously recorded video from an Amazon Kinesis Video Streams stream in a standard third-party web player, and the team does not want to build a custom player.
Which capability should the team use?
choices: Kinesis Video Streams WebRTC signaling channels
The Kinesis Video Streams GetMedia API in a custom application
The Kinesis Video Streams kvssink GStreamer plugin
Kinesis Video Streams HLS streaming sessions
explanation: HLS is an industry-standard streaming protocol that can show a Kinesis video stream live or as archived video. You create a streaming session URL and give it to a standard player such as Video.js or Shaka Player.

choiceExplanations.0: WebRTC signaling channels set up real-time peer-to-peer connections between a camera and its viewers. They are not for playing archived video in a standard player.
choiceExplanations.1: GetMedia is a low-latency API for building your own applications, so the team would have to build the player itself.
choiceExplanations.2: The kvssink plugin is a GStreamer element for sending video from a source into a stream, not for playing it back.

question:
A city's traffic cameras expose RTSP streams. A custom deep-learning application on Amazon EC2 must analyze the video frame by frame in real time, and investigators must later be able to retrieve footage for a specific time window from encrypted stored video.
Which service should the city use to ingest the video?
choices: Amazon Kinesis Video Streams, with the cameras' RTSP feeds as the source
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, with each video chunk sent as a data record
Amazon Data Firehose with an Amazon S3 destination
Amazon S3 with S3 Event Notifications that trigger the analysis
explanation: Kinesis Video Streams can take video from cameras over RTSP, lets applications read it frame by frame in real time, stores it for the retention period encrypted at rest, and time-indexes the stored data so footage can be retrieved by time.

choiceExplanations.1: Kinesis Data Streams carries generic data records. RTSP ingestion and time-indexed retrieval of video are Kinesis Video Streams features.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon Data Firehose buffers streaming data and delivers it to a destination. It does not give a custom application real-time, frame-by-frame access or time-indexed video retrieval.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon S3 stores objects. Analysis triggered after files are uploaded is not real-time frame-by-frame processing of a live stream.

resources.title: What is Amazon Kinesis Video Streams?

question:
A security team stores camera footage in Amazon Kinesis Video Streams. For an investigation, an analyst must download the footage between two timestamps as a single MP4 file with one API call, without writing a player or stitching fragments together.
Which Kinesis Video Streams feature meets this requirement?
choices: The Kinesis Video Streams GetMedia API
A Kinesis Video Streams HLS streaming session
The Kinesis Video Streams GetClip API
A Kinesis Video Streams MPEG-DASH streaming session
explanation: The GetClip API downloads an MP4 file that contains archived, on-demand media from a video stream over a specified time range.

choiceExplanations.0: GetMedia is a real-time, low-latency API for building your own applications. It does not return a ready-made MP4 file for a time range.
choiceExplanations.1: An HLS streaming session gives a URL for playback in a player, not a downloadable MP4 file.
choiceExplanations.3: An MPEG-DASH streaming session also gives a URL for playback in a player, not a downloadable MP4 file.

question:
Sales analysts with no data science background want dashboards that automatically flag unusual spikes in daily revenue and forecast next quarter's sales. The company prefers a managed, serverless business intelligence service with these machine learning features built in.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: Amazon Athena
AWS Glue
Amazon Quick Sight
Amazon EMR
explanation: Amazon Quick Sight is a business intelligence service whose built-in ML insights include anomaly detection and forecasting. Nontechnical users can add them to dashboards without building machine learning models.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that runs SQL on data in Amazon S3. It returns query results rather than dashboards with built-in anomaly detection and forecasting.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that discovers, prepares, moves and integrates data. It prepares data for analytics and is not the dashboard service.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon EMR is a managed cluster platform for big data frameworks such as Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark. It is not a business intelligence service with built-in forecasting.

resources.title: Gaining insights with machine learning (ML) in Amazon Quick Sight

question:
Dashboards in Amazon Quick Sight run against a very large Amazon Aurora table. They load slowly, and every dashboard view sends costly queries to the database. The team wants fast dashboard loads that do not query Aurora on each view.
What should the team use?
choices: Amazon Quick Sight direct query datasets
Amazon Quick Sight SPICE datasets
Amazon Quick Sight column-level security
Amazon Quick Sight anonymous embedding
explanation: Importing the data into SPICE, the in-memory engine of Amazon Quick Sight, makes analytical queries faster and lets the data be reused without querying the source each time. The dataset is refreshed from Aurora on demand or on a schedule.

choiceExplanations.0: With a direct query the data is not imported into SPICE, so the dashboard keeps sending its queries to the database whenever the data is opened.
choiceExplanations.2: Column-level security restricts which columns users and groups can see in a dataset. It does not change where the queries run or how fast they are.
choiceExplanations.3: Anonymous embedding delivers dashboards to users who are not registered in Quick Sight, inside an application. It does not change where the data is queried.

resources.title: Refreshing data in Amazon Quick Sight

question:
A finance team's data sits in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in private subnets with no public endpoint. Business analysts must build and share interactive dashboards from it in a browser. The company wants no BI servers to manage, and the database must stay off the public internet.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Amazon Quick Sight, connected to the database through a VPC connection
Amazon Quick Sight, after making the DB instance publicly accessible
A self-managed BI tool on Amazon EC2 instances in the same VPC as the database
Amazon Athena, with query results exported as CSV files for the analysts
explanation: A VPC connection adds elastic network interfaces in your VPC so Amazon Quick Sight can reach private databases such as Amazon RDS over a private network path, and traffic stays off the public internet. Quick Sight is a managed BI service, so there are no servers to run.

choiceExplanations.1: Making the DB instance publicly accessible exposes it, which breaks the requirement that the database stay off the public internet. A VPC connection reaches the private database without that.
choiceExplanations.2: A BI tool that the company installs and runs on EC2 instances means servers to manage, which the company wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that runs SQL queries. Exporting CSV files does not give analysts shareable interactive dashboards.

resources.title: Configuring VPC connections in Amazon Quick Sight

question:
A SaaS provider embeds Amazon Quick Sight dashboards in its customer portal. Thousands of customers sign in with the provider's own login system, and none of them has a Quick Sight user. Each customer must see only the rows that belong to its company, and the provider does not want to create and manage a Quick Sight user for every customer.
Which Amazon Quick Sight option meets these requirements?
choices: Amazon Quick Sight registered-user embedding, with a Quick Sight user created for each customer
Amazon Quick Sight 1-click public embedding, with the dashboards shared on the portal
Amazon Quick Sight user-based row-level security, with a permissions dataset that lists every customer
Amazon Quick Sight anonymous embedding, with tag-based row-level security
explanation: Anonymous embedding delivers dashboards without registering users in Quick Sight. Tag-based row-level security filters each dataset using session tags passed when the dashboard is embedded, so every customer sees only its own rows.

choiceExplanations.0: Registered-user embedding requires user setup, so a Quick Sight user would have to be created for each customer, which the provider wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.1: 1-click public embedding is meant for public portals and does not support row-level security, so customers could not be limited to their own rows.
choiceExplanations.2: User-based rules secure data for users and groups that are provisioned in Quick Sight. The customers here are not registered users, so tag-based rules are the option for embedded dashboards.

resources.title: Using row-level security in Amazon Quick

question:
A company wants to build a data lake in Amazon S3 from its Amazon RDS databases and one on-premises database, catalog the data, and give analysts governed self-service access through Amazon Athena, with as few manual steps as possible.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: AWS Database Migration Service
AWS Glue DataBrew
Amazon EMR
AWS Lake Formation
explanation: AWS Lake Formation helps set up a data lake: it imports data from Amazon RDS and, through JDBC, on-premises databases, catalogs it, and gives one place to manage access for analytics services such as Athena.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DMS migrates data stores and replicates changes between a source and a target. It moves data, whereas the stem also needs cataloging and governed analyst access.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool for cleaning and normalizing data. It does not build a data lake or manage access to it.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon EMR is a managed cluster platform for big data frameworks such as Hadoop and Spark. It is not the service that sets up and governs a data lake.

question:
A data lake catalog holds hundreds of tables, and new ones appear every week. The team wants each business unit's analysts to get access to every table labeled with their unit, including future tables, without writing a separate grant for each table.
Which AWS Lake Formation feature should the team use?
choices: Lake Formation tag-based access control with LF-Tags
Lake Formation named-resource grants
Lake Formation data filters
Lake Formation hybrid access mode
explanation: With tag-based access control you attach LF-Tags to databases and tables and grant principals access to tag values. Tables inherit tags from their database, so a few grants cover many current and future tables.

choiceExplanations.1: Named-resource grants name each database or table explicitly, so every table needs its own grant for every principal, which is the effort the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: A data filter belongs to one specific table and limits the columns and rows returned for a grant on it. It does not grant access across many tables by label.
choiceExplanations.3: Hybrid access mode lets you turn on Lake Formation permissions selectively for some users alongside IAM permissions. It does not group tables by label.

question:
A retail group keeps its S3 data lake and AWS Glue Data Catalog in a central account. Analysts in 30 other accounts of the same AWS Organization must query selected tables with Athena, with the credit-card columns hidden. The central team must manage all permissions in one place, without copying data or editing a bucket policy in every account.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Replicate the bucket into each analyst account with Amazon S3 replication, and remove the credit-card columns from every copy
Add the analyst accounts to the bucket policy, and give the analysts IAM roles with read access to the table's objects
Use AWS Lake Formation to grant cross-account permissions on the shared catalog tables, excluding the credit-card columns
Run Amazon Macie in every account to find the credit-card data, and rely on its findings to stop analysts reading it
explanation: Lake Formation can grant permissions on Data Catalog tables, with optional column filtering, to other accounts. It shares them through AWS RAM, so the data stays in place and the central team keeps managing permissions.

choiceExplanations.0: S3 replication copies objects into other buckets. That creates the data copies the company wants to avoid and leaves permissions to be managed in every account.
choiceExplanations.1: Bucket policies and IAM roles are set per account and apply to S3 objects, not to individual columns of a table. The column-level restriction is a Lake Formation permission.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data and generates findings. It reports on the data and does not grant or filter access to table columns.

resources.title: Cross-account data sharing in Lake Formation

question:
Analysts in a company's EU office query the orders table in the data lake with Amazon Athena. They must not see the customer_name column, and they must see only rows where the region column equals EU. A data lake administrator will grant the analysts SELECT through a Lake Formation data filter.
Which TWO settings must the data filter contain? (Choose TWO.)
choices: A Lake Formation LF-Tag expression that assigns the value EU to the orders table
A Lake Formation column specification that excludes the customer_name column
A Lake Formation resource link to the orders table in the analysts' account
A Lake Formation row filter expression that matches region = 'EU'
A Lake Formation hybrid access mode opt-in for the analysts' IAM role
explanation: A data filter combines a column specification and a row filter expression. Excluding customer_name restricts the columns, and a row filter on region limits the rows; together they give cell-level security.

choiceExplanations.0: LF-Tags grant permissions on Data Catalog resources by matching tag values. They do not filter individual rows or columns inside a table.
choiceExplanations.2: Resource links let integrated services such as Athena include shared (cross-account) resources in queries. They do not filter columns or rows.
choiceExplanations.4: Hybrid access mode lets Lake Formation permissions be enabled selectively for some users alongside IAM permissions. It does not restrict columns or rows by itself.

resources.title: Data filtering and cell-level security in Lake Formation

question:
A research institute wants to give a partner company's AWS account time-limited access to a curated data set. The partner should accept the request, and the institute does not want to build or run its own data delivery and entitlement system.
Which AWS service should the institute use?
choices: AWS DataSync
AWS Data Exchange
Amazon AppFlow
AWS Transfer Family
explanation: With AWS Data Exchange, the sender creates a data grant for the receiver's AWS account. The receiver accepts it to get access for the period the sender sets, and the sender needs no delivery or entitlement infrastructure of its own.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DataSync transfers file or object data to, from and between storage services. It does not manage time-limited entitlements that a receiver accepts.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon AppFlow exchanges data between SaaS applications and AWS services. It is not a service for granting a partner access to a data set.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Transfer Family transfers files over protocols such as SFTP and FTPS. The institute would still have to manage who has access and for how long.

question:
A company subscribed to a file-based product in AWS Data Exchange. Whenever the provider publishes a new revision, the files must appear in the company's Amazon S3 bucket without anyone starting an export.
Which AWS Data Exchange capability meets this requirement?
choices: AWS Data Exchange manual export of each revision
AWS Data Exchange data dictionaries and samples
AWS Data Exchange auto-export of new revisions
AWS Data Exchange Open Data on AWS data sets
explanation: A subscriber to a file-based product can choose to automatically export new revisions to Amazon S3 buckets when the provider publishes them, so nobody has to start each export.

choiceExplanations.0: Manual export means someone exports each revision or asset individually, which the company wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.1: Data dictionaries and samples let a prospective subscriber evaluate a product before subscribing. They do not deliver new revisions.
choiceExplanations.3: Open Data on AWS data sets are free to use without a subscription. They do not copy new revisions of a subscribed product into your bucket.

resources.title: Product subscriptions in AWS Data Exchange
Subscribing to and accessing an AWS Data Exchange product containing file-based data

question:
A company's analysts need to query a third-party provider's tables from their own Amazon Redshift cluster, read-only, without building an ETL pipeline. The charges must appear on the company's AWS bill, and access should end when the subscription ends.
Which solution should the company choose?
choices: An AWS Glue ETL job that copies the provider's tables into the cluster every night
AWS DMS replicating the provider's database into the cluster continuously
AWS DataSync copying the provider's exported files to Amazon S3 for loading into the cluster
A subscription through AWS Data Exchange to a product that contains an Amazon Redshift data set
explanation: An AWS Data Exchange product with an Amazon Redshift data set gives subscribers read-only access to the provider's datashares, so they query the data without ETL. Paid subscriptions are billed on the AWS bill, and access to the datashares is lost when the subscription expires.

choiceExplanations.0: A Glue ETL job is the kind of pipeline the company wants to avoid. It copies the data into the cluster, and nothing in it ends access when a subscription ends.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS DMS is a migration and replication service that runs a replication task between a source and a target. It would copy the data into the cluster instead of giving subscription-based read-only access.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS DataSync transfers file or object data between storage services. The files would still have to be loaded into Redshift, which is the pipeline the company wants to avoid.

resources.title: Subscribing to and accessing an AWS Data Exchange product containing Amazon Redshift data sets

question:
A data science team subscribed to a licensed data set that a provider stores as large files in the provider's own Amazon S3 bucket. The team wants to analyze the files with Amazon Athena where they are, with no copy in the team's own buckets and no export jobs.
Which AWS Data Exchange data set type supports this?
choices: AWS Data Exchange for Amazon S3 data access
AWS Data Exchange Files data sets with auto-export to the team's bucket
AWS Data Exchange API data sets that are called through Amazon API Gateway
AWS Data Exchange Files data sets downloaded through jobs with signed URLs
explanation: AWS Data Exchange for Amazon S3 lets subscribers use the provider's files directly in the provider's Amazon S3 buckets with services such as Athena or Amazon EMR. Data Exchange provisions an S3 access point that grants the subscriber read-only access.

choiceExplanations.1: Auto-export copies each new revision into the team's own bucket, which is the copy the team wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: API data sets let subscribers call the provider's API. They do not expose the provider's files in Amazon S3 for Athena to query.
choiceExplanations.3: Signed-URL jobs download or export file assets from a Files data set. That is an export job and creates a copy, which the team wants to avoid.

resources.title: Subscribing to and accessing an AWS Data Exchange product containing Amazon S3 data access

question:
An operations team runs open-source Grafana on Amazon EC2 instances to chart CloudWatch and Prometheus metrics. Patching and scaling the Grafana servers takes too much time, but the team wants to keep using Grafana dashboards.
Which AWS service should the team use?
choices: Amazon Managed Grafana
Amazon Quick Sight
AWS X-Ray
Amazon OpenSearch Service
explanation: Amazon Managed Grafana runs Grafana as a managed service. It handles provisioning, setup, scaling and maintenance of the Grafana servers, and it integrates with sources such as Amazon CloudWatch and Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus.

choiceExplanations.1: Amazon Quick Sight is a data visualization and business intelligence service. It is not managed Grafana, so the team would have to rebuild its Grafana dashboards.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS X-Ray collects data about requests that an application serves, as traces. It is not a dashboard service for Grafana.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon OpenSearch Service runs managed OpenSearch clusters for search and analytics such as log analytics. It does not host Grafana.

question:
An Amazon Managed Grafana workspace must chart data from an Amazon Redshift cluster that runs in private subnets. The company will not make the cluster publicly accessible.
Which capability should the team configure?
choices: Amazon Managed Grafana network access control with a managed prefix list
Amazon Managed Grafana service-managed permissions for the account
Amazon Managed Grafana connection to the VPC that hosts the cluster
Amazon Managed Grafana authentication through SAML 2.0
explanation: A workspace reaches data sources over the public internet by default. Connecting the workspace to the VPC creates network interfaces in the VPC's subnets, and all traffic then flows through the VPC, so private data sources can be used.

choiceExplanations.0: Network access control decides which requests may reach the workspace, by IP prefix list or VPC endpoint. It does not give the workspace a path to a private data source.
choiceExplanations.1: Service-managed permissions create the IAM roles and policies the workspace needs to use AWS data sources. They do not change the network path.
choiceExplanations.3: SAML 2.0 is one way for users to sign in to a workspace. It does not affect how the workspace connects to data sources.

resources.title: Connect to data sources or notification channels in Amazon VPC from Amazon Managed Grafana

question:
A gaming company runs Kubernetes on Amazon EKS and on self-managed EC2 clusters. Its platform engineers write PromQL queries and want one set of dashboards and alerts for the container metrics. They sign in through a corporate SAML 2.0 identity provider, and the company wants to run no Prometheus or Grafana servers itself.
Which solution should the company use?
choices: Prometheus and Grafana installed on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus for the metrics and Amazon Managed Grafana for the dashboards
Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards, fed by log shippers on every node
AWS X-Ray with its trace map for every service that the clusters run
explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a serverless, Prometheus-compatible service that works with EKS and self-managed Kubernetes and uses PromQL. Amazon Managed Grafana provides the dashboards and signs users in through SAML 2.0 identity providers, and neither needs servers to run.

choiceExplanations.0: Prometheus and Grafana on EC2 instances means the company installs, patches and scales the servers, which it wants to avoid.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a search and analytics engine for use cases such as log analytics, not a Prometheus-compatible store that runs PromQL queries over container metrics.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS X-Ray collects trace data about the requests an application serves. It does not store container metrics or run PromQL queries.

resources.title: What is Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?

question:
A central observability workspace in Amazon Managed Grafana was created in the organization's delegated administrator account. It must read CloudWatch metrics from member accounts in several organizational units, and the cloud team wants the LEAST administrative effort to create the IAM roles in those accounts.
Which permission setup should the team choose?
choices: Amazon Managed Grafana service-managed permissions for the current account
Amazon Managed Grafana service-managed permissions for the organization
Amazon Managed Grafana customer-managed permissions, with a role created by hand in each member account
Amazon Managed Grafana network access control that allows the IP ranges of each member account
explanation: In service-managed permissions for the organization, Amazon Managed Grafana creates the IAM roles it needs in each account of the organizational units you select, using CloudFormation StackSets. This mode is supported for workspaces created in a management or delegated administrator account.

choiceExplanations.0: This mode creates a service role for the workspace's own account. It is not the mode that sets up roles in the other accounts of the organization.
choiceExplanations.2: With customer-managed permissions you create and trust the roles in every member account yourself, which is more administrative effort than letting the service create them.
choiceExplanations.3: Network access control only filters which requests may reach the workspace. It grants no permission to read data in other accounts.

resources.title: Amazon Managed Grafana permissions and policies for AWS data sources

question:
A platform team runs Prometheus servers on EC2 instances to scrape its Kubernetes clusters. Storage keeps filling up, and a server failure once lost recent data. The team wants to keep its existing PromQL queries and not manage any servers.
Which AWS service should the team use?
choices: Amazon Managed Grafana
AWS X-Ray
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is serverless and Prometheus-compatible, so teams keep the Prometheus data model and PromQL. It scales ingestion and storage automatically and replicates ingested data across three Availability Zones.

choiceExplanations.0: Amazon Managed Grafana visualizes data from sources such as Prometheus workspaces. It is not the store that ingests and keeps the Prometheus metrics.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS X-Ray collects trace data about requests to an application. It does not store Prometheus metrics or run PromQL.
choiceExplanations.2: Amazon OpenSearch Service runs managed OpenSearch clusters for search and analytics. It is not a Prometheus-compatible service for PromQL queries.

resources.title: What is Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?

question:
A team runs workloads on Amazon EKS and sends cluster metrics to an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace. The team does not want to install, run or maintain any collector agents, and it does not want to change application code.
Which ingestion option meets these requirements?
choices: A Prometheus server in agent mode that remote-writes to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
An AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry collector that remote-writes to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
An AWS managed collector that scrapes the EKS cluster for Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
Application code that remote-writes its metrics straight to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
explanation: An AWS managed collector is a fully managed, agentless scraper that pulls Prometheus-compatible metrics from an Amazon EKS cluster into the workspace. The team installs and maintains nothing, and the applications stay unchanged.

choiceExplanations.0: A Prometheus server running in agent mode is a customer managed collector. The team must run it and keep ingestion available.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry is another customer managed collector option, so the team would still deploy and maintain the agents.
choiceExplanations.3: Sending metrics with remote write from the application's own code means changing the application, which the team does not want to do.

resources.title: Ingest metrics to your Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace
Set up managed collectors for Amazon EKS

question:
An audit rule requires 24 months of container performance metrics from several EKS clusters to stay queryable with PromQL. The platform team will not manage any storage or servers.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, with the workspace retention period set to 730 days
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, with the default workspace retention period
A Prometheus server on Amazon EC2 with a large Amazon EBS volume for local storage
An Amazon OpenSearch Service domain with UltraWarm storage for the older metrics
explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus stores metrics for 150 days by default, and you can set the workspace retention period to a maximum of 1095 days. A 730-day setting covers 24 months without storage or servers to manage.

choiceExplanations.1: The default retention is 150 days, after which metrics are deleted automatically, so it does not cover 24 months.
choiceExplanations.2: A Prometheus server on EC2 means the team sizes and manages the instance and its storage, which it will not do.
choiceExplanations.3: An OpenSearch Service domain is a cluster of instances with storage that you size. It is not a Prometheus-compatible service for PromQL queries.

resources.title: What is Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?

question:
A company plans to move the container monitoring for its Amazon EKS clusters to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus. The architect reviews statements about the service.
Which TWO statements are correct? (Choose TWO.)
choices: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus makes the team size and add storage as the metrics grow
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus queries metrics with SQL instead of PromQL
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus replicates the data ingested into a workspace across three Availability Zones
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus works only with clusters that run on Amazon EKS
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus lets the team change how long metrics are kept, up to three years
explanation: Data ingested into a workspace is replicated across three Availability Zones in the Region. Metrics are kept for 150 days by default, and the retention period can be configured up to a maximum of 1095 days (three years).

choiceExplanations.0: The service automatically scales ingestion, storage and querying as workloads scale, so the team does not size storage.
choiceExplanations.1: The service uses the open-source Prometheus data model and the PromQL query language, not SQL.
choiceExplanations.3: The service works with container clusters on Amazon EKS and with self-managed Kubernetes environments, so it is not limited to EKS.

resources.title: What is Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?

question:
A cloud team wants data-driven recommendations for the memory size of its AWS Lambda functions and for the instance types of its EC2 Auto Scaling groups, based on the resources' utilization history in Amazon CloudWatch.
Which AWS service should the team use?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes configuration and CloudWatch utilization metrics and gives rightsizing recommendations. It covers Lambda function memory sizes and EC2 Auto Scaling groups, among other resources.

choiceExplanations.0: The rightsizing recommendations feature in AWS Cost Explorer analyzes Amazon EC2 instances. It does not cover Lambda function memory sizes.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Config records the configuration of resources and how it changes over time. It does not recommend memory sizes or instance types.
choiceExplanations.3: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. It does not make sizing recommendations.

question:
A team wants a list of its EC2 instances that are too small for their workloads and risk poor application performance. The team has opted in to AWS Compute Optimizer.
Which Compute Optimizer result should the team filter for?
choices: Compute Optimizer over-provisioned findings
Compute Optimizer optimized findings
Compute Optimizer enhanced infrastructure metrics
Compute Optimizer under-provisioned findings
explanation: Compute Optimizer classifies an EC2 instance as under-provisioned when at least one specification, such as CPU, memory or network, does not meet the workload's performance requirements. Such instances might lead to poor application performance.

choiceExplanations.0: Over-provisioned means at least one specification can be sized down while still meeting the workload's needs, so it points to unnecessary cost, not performance risk.
choiceExplanations.1: Optimized means all specifications meet the workload's performance requirements and the instance is not over-provisioned, so these instances are not too small.
choiceExplanations.2: Enhanced infrastructure metrics is a paid preference that extends the lookback period of the analysis. It is not a finding classification.

question:
A central FinOps team must find over-provisioned EC2 instances, Lambda functions, EBS volumes and Amazon ECS services on AWS Fargate across all 60 accounts of its AWS Organization. The team wants one place to review the findings, and it prefers to use the utilization data that AWS services already publish to CloudWatch.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: AWS Cost Explorer rightsizing recommendations in the management account
AWS Budgets usage budgets created for every account in the organization
AWS Compute Optimizer, opted in from the management account for all accounts in the organization
AWS Config, recording the resource configurations in every account of the organization
explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes EC2 instances, Lambda functions, EBS volumes and ECS services on Fargate from CloudWatch metrics. Opting in the management account with all accounts in the organization gives findings and recommendations across the accounts.

choiceExplanations.0: Rightsizing recommendations in Cost Explorer identify underutilized Amazon EC2 instances, so Lambda functions, EBS volumes and Fargate services are not covered.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Budgets tracks costs and usage against targets and sends alerts. It does not analyze utilization to find over-provisioned resources.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Config records resource configurations and how they change. It does not analyze utilization metrics to recommend smaller sizes.

resources.title: Opting in to AWS Compute Optimizer

question:
A media company's EC2 batch cluster is nearly idle except for a heavy job on the last day of each month. AWS Compute Optimizer flags the instances as over-provisioned, but the team fears the analysis looked at a quiet period and that downsizing would break the month-end job.
Which Compute Optimizer feature gives the analysis a longer history of utilization data?
choices: Compute Optimizer enhanced infrastructure metrics
Compute Optimizer with the CloudWatch agent installed to report memory utilization
Compute Optimizer exports of recommendations to Amazon S3
Compute Optimizer opt-in for all accounts in the organization
explanation: Compute Optimizer normally analyzes the last 14 days of utilization. The paid enhanced infrastructure metrics preference extends the lookback period for EC2 instances to up to 93 days, so a month-end peak is included.

choiceExplanations.1: The CloudWatch agent adds memory utilization data for the analysis. It does not lengthen the 14-day lookback period.
choiceExplanations.2: Exports record recommendations over time and let you share them. They do not change how much utilization history the analysis uses.
choiceExplanations.3: Opting in all accounts widens which accounts are analyzed. It does not extend the lookback period.

resources.title: Metrics analyzed by AWS Compute Optimizer

question:
A retail company keeps its order data in an on-premises Oracle database that must stay online. It wants the data copied to Amazon Redshift for analytics, with later changes replicated continuously, and without writing custom code.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family
AWS DMS
AWS Storage Gateway
explanation: AWS DMS migrates databases to AWS while the source database stays operational, and it can keep replicating ongoing changes to targets such as Amazon Redshift, so no custom code is needed.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DataSync transfers files and objects between storage systems; it does not read database tables or replicate database changes.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Transfer Family gives clients SFTP, FTPS and FTP access to Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS; it does not migrate or replicate databases.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to cloud-backed storage; it does not replicate a relational database into a data warehouse.

resources.title: What is AWS Database Migration Service?
Creating tasks for ongoing replication using AWS DMS

question:
A company runs a long-lived AWS DMS task that replicates changes from a production MySQL database to Amazon Aurora. The replication must continue with little or no interruption if the Availability Zone that hosts the replication instance fails.
Which option should the company use?
choices: An AWS DMS replication instance with a larger instance class
An AWS DMS replication instance with the Multi-AZ option
An AWS DMS task with data validation turned on
An AWS DMS task that uses the CDC-only migration type
explanation: With the Multi-AZ option, AWS DMS provisions and maintains a synchronous standby replica of the replication instance in a different Availability Zone, so replication can fail over with little or no interruption.

choiceExplanations.0: A larger instance class adds CPU and memory, but the replication instance still runs in one Availability Zone, so a failure of that zone still stops replication.
choiceExplanations.2: Data validation compares source rows with target rows after they are migrated; it does not add a standby replication instance.
choiceExplanations.3: The CDC-only migration type decides which data the task replicates (changes made after the initial load); it does not change how the replication instance is deployed.

resources.title: Working with an AWS DMS replication instance

question:
A payments processor records every transaction in a Microsoft SQL Server database in its own data center. A fraud-detection application on AWS must receive each committed row change as a record on an Amazon Kinesis data stream, continuously. The database must stay in service, and the team can neither modify the transaction application nor add triggers to the database.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: An AWS DMS ongoing replication (CDC) task that reads changes from the SQL Server transaction log and writes them to the Kinesis data stream
A full-load-only AWS DMS task that is re-run on a schedule, with the Kinesis data stream as its target
An AWS Glue job that connects to the database over JDBC every minute and writes the table contents to the stream
The Amazon Kinesis Producer Library added to the transaction application to publish each change to the stream
explanation: An AWS DMS ongoing replication (CDC) task captures changes from the source database's transaction log, so no triggers or application changes are needed, and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is a supported AWS DMS target. The source database stays in service while the task runs.

choiceExplanations.1: A full-load task copies the current contents of the tables each time it runs; it does not read the change log, so it cannot deliver each committed row change as it happens.
choiceExplanations.2: A scheduled JDBC job reads table contents at intervals; it does not read the transaction log, so it cannot deliver each individual committed change.
choiceExplanations.3: The Kinesis Producer Library is used inside an application to write records, so using it here means changing the transaction application, which the team cannot do.

resources.title: Creating tasks for ongoing replication using AWS DMS
Using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams as a target for AWS Database Migration Service

question:
A team will run an AWS DMS full-load-and-CDC task from Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Before the task runs, it wants AWS DMS to flag unsupported data types and other problems with the task. After the data is loaded, it wants AWS DMS to compare each source row with its target row and report mismatches.
Which TWO AWS DMS features should the team use? (Choose TWO.)
choices: An AWS DMS premigration assessment run for the task
An AWS DMS replication instance with the Multi-AZ option
AWS DMS data validation turned on in the task settings
AWS DMS table-mapping transformation rules applied to the selected tables
AWS DMS task logging at a detailed severity level in Amazon CloudWatch Logs
explanation: A premigration assessment run evaluates a task before it starts, for example which source data types can or cannot be migrated. Data validation then compares each row in the source with the corresponding row at the target and reports any mismatches.

choiceExplanations.1: Multi-AZ adds a standby replication instance for availability; it neither assesses a task before it runs nor compares rows.
choiceExplanations.3: Transformation rules are optional changes (such as adding a column or changing a data type) applied to selected schemas, tables or views; they do not check readiness or verify migrated data.
choiceExplanations.4: Task logging writes component activity to CloudWatch Logs at the severity you choose, which helps with troubleshooting; it does not assess a task in advance or compare source and target rows.

resources.title: Enabling and working with premigration assessments for a task

question:
A research team collects sensor and imaging data on a ship that has no internet connection for weeks. It wants to process part of the data on board and then get all of it into Amazon S3 without using a network link.
Which AWS service should the team use?
choices: AWS DataSync
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Storage Gateway
AWS Snow Family
explanation: AWS Snow Family devices are rugged physical devices that can store and process data at the edge. They are shipped to AWS, which imports the data into Amazon S3 without using the internet.

choiceExplanations.0: AWS DataSync moves data over a network connection, so it cannot transfer the data from a ship that has no connectivity.
choiceExplanations.1: AWS Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection between a facility and AWS; it needs a physical network link, which a ship at sea does not have.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Storage Gateway gives on-premises applications access to cloud storage over a network connection, so it cannot move data without connectivity.

question:
A company keeps its video archive in Amazon S3 and must copy all of it into a new on-premises data center that has a slow internet connection. It will use AWS Snow Family devices for the offline transfer.
Which type of Snow Family job should the company create?
choices: A Snow Family import job into Amazon S3
A Snow Family export job from Amazon S3
A Snow Family local compute and storage job on one device
A Snow Family local compute and storage job on a cluster of devices
explanation: An export job copies data from Amazon S3 onto one or more Snow devices, which are shipped to the company's location so the data can be copied into the data center.

choiceExplanations.0: An import job works in the opposite direction: it copies on-premises data onto a device that is shipped to AWS and imported into Amazon S3.
choiceExplanations.2: A local compute and storage job does not start with data from Amazon S3 buckets, unlike an export job.
choiceExplanations.3: A cluster is an option for local compute and storage jobs, which do not start with data from Amazon S3 buckets; clustering adds durability, not an export of S3 data.

resources.title: Jobs to export data from Amazon S3 using a Snowball Edge device

question:
A genomics lab has 150 TB of sequencing output on local storage, and its 100 Mbps internet link is shared with other departments. The data must be archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive within three weeks at the lowest cost.
As the solutions architect, which approach should you recommend?
choices: Install an AWS DataSync agent and run a task over the shared link, with S3 Glacier Deep Archive as the destination storage class
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on a bucket and upload the files with multipart uploads straight into S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Order AWS Snow Family devices for an import job into an S3 bucket, then use an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway and have the backup software write virtual tapes over the shared link
explanation: Even an idle 100 Mbps link would need more than four months to move 150 TB, so every online option misses the three-week deadline. A Snow Family import job moves the data physically into Amazon S3, and a lifecycle rule then transitions the objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

choiceExplanations.0: DataSync can write to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, but it still sends all 150 TB over the 100 Mbps shared link, which is far too slow for the deadline.
choiceExplanations.1: Transfer Acceleration speeds up long-distance uploads over the internet, but every byte still has to leave the lab through its 100 Mbps link.
choiceExplanations.3: A tape gateway also sends the data to AWS over the network, so the same shared 100 Mbps link limits it.

resources.title: Jobs to import data into Amazon S3 using a Snowball Edge device
Uploading an Archive in Amazon Glacier

question:
A mining company needs S3-compatible storage and Amazon EC2-compatible compute at a remote site that will have no connectivity for several months. The data will not be uploaded to AWS afterward, and it must remain available if one device fails.
Which TWO choices should the company make when ordering AWS Snow Family devices? (Choose TWO.)
choices: A Snow Family import job
A Snow Family export job
A Snow Family local compute and storage job
A single Snow Family device with S3-compatible storage
A cluster of at least three Snow Family devices
explanation: A local compute and storage job keeps the data on the devices and runs compute locally, with no import into Amazon S3 when the devices are returned. Ordering it as a cluster of three or more devices makes the data more durable, because a cluster can lose a device and keep the data.

choiceExplanations.0: An import job is meant to be returned so its data is imported into Amazon S3, which the company does not want, and each import job has exactly one device.
choiceExplanations.1: An export job copies data from Amazon S3 onto devices; the cluster option belongs to local compute and storage jobs.
choiceExplanations.3: A single device has no redundancy across devices, so a device failure puts the data on it at risk.

resources.title: Information about using Snowball Edge devices to provide local compute and storage functionality
Using Amazon S3 compatible storage on Snowball Edge with a cluster of Snow devices

question:
A media company stores 40 TB of video files in Microsoft Azure Blob Storage. It wants to copy them to Amazon S3, rerun the copy on a schedule until the final switch, and avoid writing custom transfer scripts.
Which AWS service should the company use?
choices: AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family
AWS Storage Gateway
AWS Application Migration Service
explanation: AWS DataSync can transfer data between Microsoft Azure Blob Storage and Amazon S3, and a DataSync task can run on a schedule, so no custom scripts are needed.

choiceExplanations.1: AWS Transfer Family gives clients SFTP, FTPS and FTP access to Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS; it is not a tool for copying a data set out of another cloud's storage.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to cloud-backed storage; it is not designed to copy a data set out of Azure Blob Storage.
choiceExplanations.3: AWS Application Migration Service rehosts servers on Amazon EC2; it does not copy object storage.

resources.title: Configuring transfers with Microsoft Azure Blob Storage
Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs

question:
A company copies files from an on-premises NFS server to Amazon S3 with AWS DataSync over an internet link that business applications also use. The transfer must keep running during business hours, but it must not use all of the available bandwidth.
Which DataSync option should the company configure?
choices: A DataSync task schedule that starts transfers only at night
A DataSync task bandwidth limit
A DataSync task option to transfer only data that has changed
A DataSync task option to verify only the transferred data
explanation: A DataSync task bandwidth limit caps the network bandwidth that each task execution can use, and the limit can even be changed while an execution is running.

choiceExplanations.0: A schedule only controls when a task starts; running only at night would not let the transfer continue during business hours.
choiceExplanations.2: Transferring only changed data reduces how much data later runs copy, but each run can still use all of the available bandwidth.
choiceExplanations.3: Verification checks data integrity at the end of a transfer; it does not limit how much bandwidth the transfer uses.

resources.title: Setting bandwidth limits for your AWS DataSync task

question:
A reporting application writes daily export files to an Amazon EFS file system in us-east-1. Each night, new and changed files must be copied, with their file metadata, to an Amazon S3 bucket in eu-west-1 in the same AWS account. There must be no agents or servers to manage, with the LEAST operational overhead.
Which solution meets these requirements?
choices: Amazon EFS Replication to a new EFS file system in eu-west-1 that is kept in sync with the source file system
An AWS Backup plan with a nightly rule that copies the EFS file system to a backup vault in eu-west-1
An AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoint for the file system, with a nightly script that downloads the files and uploads them to the bucket
An AWS DataSync task with the EFS file system as the source location and the S3 bucket as the destination, run on a nightly schedule
explanation: AWS DataSync copies data between AWS storage services such as Amazon EFS and Amazon S3 in the same account, including across Regions, without an agent. A scheduled task copies only new and changed data, and it keeps the files' POSIX metadata as S3 user metadata.

choiceExplanations.0: EFS Replication copies data and metadata only to another EFS file system, so the files would not arrive in an S3 bucket.
choiceExplanations.1: An AWS Backup copy creates a duplicate of the recovery point in a backup vault in another Region; it does not write the files into an S3 bucket.
choiceExplanations.2: AWS Transfer Family can use Amazon EFS, but it gives clients protocol access instead of scheduled copying, and the script adds the operational work the stem rules out.

resources.title: Understanding how DataSync handles file and object metadata

question:
A records-management team uses AWS DataSync to archive 80 TB of files from an on-premises NFS server directly into the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. Compliance requires DataSync to compare checksums of the transferred data at the end of each run.
Which verification setting should the team choose?
choices: The DataSync option to verify all data in the source and destination locations
The DataSync option to skip verification after the transfer
The DataSync option to verify only the data that was transferred
The DataSync option to transfer all data instead of only changed data
explanation: Verifying only transferred data makes DataSync calculate checksums of the transferred data at the source and compare them with the destination at the end of the transfer. It is the recommended option for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

choiceExplanations.0: Verifying all data cannot be used when the destination is S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
